title: Finite form
label: def:finite-form
statement:
A \term{finite form} $X$ consists of a finite cell set $\cells(X)$ together
with declared carried structure. Carried structure may include types, tags,
orders, incidence relations, orientations, labels, or distinguished cells.
Two forms are identical only when the data declared relevant by their type
agree.

title: Perfect alignment
label: def:perfect-alignment
statement:
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite rods. A \term{perfect alignment} is an
order-preserving bijection $\alpha:\cells(P)\to\cells(Q)$. We write
$\Align(P,Q)$ for the set of such witnesses.

title: Uniqueness of rod alignment
label: prop:rod-alignment-unique
statement:
Between two finite linearly ordered rods there is at most one perfect
alignment.

title: Rectangular tapestry
label: def:time-rectangular
statement:
Let $T:\TimeForm$ supply the temporal positions and their successor.
Let $R:\OrderedForm$ index the rows in order: each cell
$r:\cells(R)$ names one row. For every row choose a type $V_r$ of
allowed values, and write $V=(V_r)_{r:\cells(R)}$ for this family.
A \term{thread} $e_r:\cells(T)\to V_r$ assigns one allowed value
to each temporal position in row $r$. The family $e=(e_r)_r$ supplies
one such thread for every row:
\formationline{&T:\TimeForm,\quad R:\OrderedForm,\\
 &V_r\text{ a type for each }r:\cells(R),\\
 &e:\AFDepFun_{r:\cells(R)}(\cells(T)\to V_r)\\
 &\qquad\Longrightarrow\;\RectTapestry(T;R,V,e):\TapestryForm}

The constructed tapestry retains $T$, $R$, $V$ and $e$. Its addresses
are pairs $(r,t)$ in $\cells(R)\times\cells(T)$; the entry at that
address is $e_r(t):V_r$. Keeping $T$, $R$ and $V$ while leaving the
entries unspecified gives its \term{frame}, written
$A_{\mathrm{rect}}(T;R,V)$.

title: Occurrence history
label: def:time-history
statement:
\index{occurrence history}
A transition graph $G$ supplies states, named transitions, and the source
and target of each transition. A finite history
$\gamma=(x_0,a_0,x_1,\ldots,a_{H-1},x_H)$ lists $H$ transitions
whose endpoints fit; write $\mathsf{Path}_H(G)$ for the type of such
histories. Its $H+1$ occurrence positions form
$I_H=\LinearTime(H+1)$. The state at position $i$ is $h(i)=x_i$.
\formationline{&G,\quad \gamma:\mathsf{Path}_H(G)\\
 &\qquad\Longrightarrow\;\OccurrenceHistory(G;\gamma):
       \mathsf{OccurrenceHistoryData}(G)}
This record retains the positions and their transitions, including
repeated uses of the same transition. The projection $h$ reads the state
at each position and may give the same state at different positions.

title: Tick realization
label: def:time-ticks
statement:
\index{tick realization}
Let $S_G$ be the state set of a transition graph $G$, and let $T$ be a
pointed cycle with successor $s$ and base phase $t_0$.
A tick realization retains a phase projection
$q:S_G\to\cells(T)$, an initial state $x_0\in S_G$,
and a label $\kappa(a)\in\{0,1\}$ for each admitted transition.
The label says whether that transition registers a tick. A certificate
checks the corresponding equation:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 \kappa(a)=0&q(x')=q(x)\\
 \kappa(a)=1&q(x')=s(q(x))
\end{array}
\qquad (a:x\longrightarrow x').
\]
Writing $\ell$ for these data and $c$ for their certificate gives
\formationline{&\ell:\mathsf{TickData}(G,T),\quad
 c:\mathsf{TickLaw}(\ell)\\
 &\qquad\Longrightarrow\;(\ell,c):\TickRealization(G,T)}
The initial phase must satisfy $q(x_0)=t_0$.

title: Finite cyclarchy
label: def:time-cyclarchy
statement:
Let $N=(N_1,\ldots,N_r)$ be a nonempty list of radices, with
$N_i\ge2$. Put $P_0=1$ and $P_k=N_1\cdots N_k$.
A \term{cyclarchy} with this radix list retains the digit states
\[
 S_N=\prod_{i=1}^r\{0,\ldots,N_i-1\},
 \qquad 0_N=(0,\ldots,0),
\]
and addition with carry, starting at the least significant digit $a_1$.
To add $a$ and $b$, set $c_0=0$ and, successively for $i=1,\ldots,r$,
\[
 u_i=a_i+b_i+c_{i-1},\qquad
 (a\oplus b)_i=u_i\bmod N_i,\qquad
 c_i=\lfloor u_i/N_i\rfloor.
\]
Discard the final carry $c_r$. The unit increment adds $(1,0,\ldots,0)$.
The retained checkpoint levels mark multiples of $P_k$ increments from
zero: at such a checkpoint the lowest $k$ digits are all zero.
\formationline{&N=(N_1,\ldots,N_r),\quad r\ge1,\quad N_i\ge2\\
 &\qquad\Longrightarrow\;\Cyclarchy(N):\mathsf{CyclarchyData}(N)}

title: Interpretation witness
label: def:intwit-book
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an interpretation profile, $F$ a raw artform and
$\theta$ an endpoint of $\mathcal C$. An \term{interpretation witness} of
$\theta$ from $F$ under $\mathcal C$ is a pair $w=(\ell,c)$: a realizer
$\ell$ of $\mathcal C$ together with a \term{certificate} $c$, evidence in
a form that can be checked that $\ell$ produces $\theta$ from $F$ and obeys
the law of $\mathcal C$. We write $\IntWit_{\mathcal C}(F,\theta)$ for the
set of such witnesses, as $\Align(P,Q)$ in \cref{sec:rods-grids} is the
set of perfect alignments. If $\Gamma$ lists the profiles in use, the
\term{semantic fibre} $\Sem_\Gamma(F)$ of $F$ is the set of tagged
witnesses $(\mathcal C,\theta,w)$ with $\mathcal C$ a profile of $\Gamma$
that applies to $F$, $\theta$ an endpoint of $\mathcal C$ and
$w\in\IntWit_{\mathcal C}(F,\theta)$: every witness of every available
profile, each carrying the tag of its profile. The fibre stands beside $F$
and selects nothing. Choosing one tagged witness and carrying it with $F$
is a further step; we write $\PointedInt_\Gamma$ for the set of such pairs
$(F,(\mathcal C,\theta,w))$, the selected layer. None of these
constructions changes raw artform equality.

title: The two tetractys interpretations coexist
label: prop:tetractys-intwits
statement:
Let $P$ be the ten-cell palette with row sizes $k=1,2,3,4$, and write the
phases in each row locally as $0,\ldots,k-1$. On the common clock
$t\in\{0,\ldots,11\}$, the two laying rules are
\begin{equation}
 \ell_{\mathrm{rec}}(k,t)=t\bmod k,
 \qquad
 \ell_{\mathrm{div}}(k,t)=\left\lfloor\frac{kt}{12}\right\rfloor.
 
\end{equation}
There are profiles $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$ and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{div}}$
whose laws are respectively the covering and the grouping equation, the
phase typing and the period spectra $\{\!\{1,2,3,4\}\!\}$ and
$\{\!\{1,12,12,12\}\!\}$. Consequently
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 w_{\mathrm{rec}}&=(\ell_{\mathrm{rec}},c_{\mathrm{rec}})
   \in\IntWit_{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}}(P,I_{\mathrm{rec}}),\\
 w_{\mathrm{div}}&=(\ell_{\mathrm{div}},c_{\mathrm{div}})
   \in\IntWit_{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{div}}}(P,I_{\mathrm{div}}),
 \end{aligned}
\]
and tagging each witness with its profile and endpoint gives two
elements of $\Sem_\Gamma(P)$ whenever $\Gamma$ lists the two profiles.

title: Finite cell pattern
label: def:finite-cell-pattern
section: Constructing a space and its states
statement:
A finite cell pattern has typed vertex, edge, face, and possibly higher-cell
sets, its \term{grading}, together with an immediate-face relation raising
dimension by one and a declared outer boundary. The boundary is \term{face-closed}:
with any cell it includes that cell's faces, their faces, and so on.
Thus an edge in the boundary brings both endpoints with it.
Local boundary data record the faces around each cell. They differ
from the outer-boundary mark: an interior square of a board has four
sides, although none need lie on the board's outside edge.
Orientation is an enrichment: an oriented
edge has a source and target.
An oriented face carries a boundary word in oriented edges. A \term{palette}
assigns allowed labels or states to selected cells, as the palette of
\cref{sec:time} listed the allowed values of each row.

title: Geometric form and its instances
label: def:geometric-form-book
section: Constructing a space and its states
statement:
A \term{geometric form} is a finite shape descriptor
$G=(P,\sigma):\AFGeometricForm$: a representative canvas $P$ and
its declared geometric profile. Its \term{instance type},
$\mathsf{Instance}(G)$, consists of canvases whose cells can be put
in bijection with those of $P$, preserving the selected structure
in both directions. A bijection is a pairing in which every cell
on each side has exactly one partner. Existence of the pairing is
the property; choosing one is additional comparison data.

title: Artform frame and instance
label: def:frame-instance
section: Constructing a space and its states
statement:
An \term{artform frame} is a typed specification of a carrier, its carried
structure, the space of legal states, the allowed observations, and the
allowed moves. An \term{artform instance} is one legal state inhabiting that
frame.

title: Category
label: def:category-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}

title: The Artform category
label: prop:artform-category-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
Finite composable lists of the declared operations form a category with
the frames as objects. Any equivalence relation on parallel lists that is
preserved by composition gives a quotient category.

title: Subcategory
label: def:subcategory-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
A \term{subcategory} $\mathcal D$ of $\mathcal C$ selects objects and
arrows of $\mathcal C$, retains the identity of every selected object,
and closes its arrows under composition. It inherits composition and
arrow equality from $\mathcal C$. It is \term{full} if it contains
every arrow of $\mathcal C$ between its selected objects.

title: Functor
label: def:functor-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
A \term{functor} $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ assigns an object
$F(A)$ to each object and an arrow $F(f):F(A)\to F(B)$ to each
arrow $f:A\to B$, preserving identities and composition:
\[
 F(1_A)=1_{F(A)},\qquad F(g\circ f)=F(g)\circ F(f).
\]

title: The semantic quotient
label: prop:semantic-quotient-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
State-equivalence is preserved by composition. The quotient of
$\mathsf{Art}^{\mathrm{syn}}$ by it is a category, and its state
interpretation is faithful: distinct arrows between the same two frames
denote distinct functions.

title: Natural transformation
label: def:natural-transformation-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
For functors $F,G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, a
\term{natural transformation} $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ assigns an
arrow $\eta_A:F(A)\to G(A)$ to every object $A$ of $\mathcal C$,
such that for every arrow $u:A\to B$,
\begin{equation}
 G(u)\circ\eta_A=\eta_B\circ F(u).
 
\end{equation}
The arrows $\eta_A$ are its components.

title: Product
label: def:product-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
A product of $A$ and $B$ is an object $A\times B$ with projections
$\pi_A:A\times B\to A$ and $\pi_B:A\times B\to B$ such that,
for every $u:Z\to A$ and $v:Z\to B$, there is exactly one arrow
$\langle u,v\rangle:Z\to A\times B$ with
\[
 \pi_A\circ\langle u,v\rangle=u,\qquad
 \pi_B\circ\langle u,v\rangle=v.
\]

title: Coproduct
label: def:coproduct-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
A coproduct of $A$ and $B$ is an object $A\sqcup B$ with maps
$\iota_A:A\to A\sqcup B$, $\iota_B:B\to A\sqcup B$ such that
for every $u:A\to Z$ and $v:B\to Z$ there is exactly one map
$[u,v]:A\sqcup B\to Z$ satisfying
$[u,v]\circ\iota_A=u$ and $[u,v]\circ\iota_B=v$.

title: Exponential
label: def:exponential-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
In a category with products, an exponential $B^A$ has an evaluation
map $\operatorname{ev}:B^A\times A\to B$ such that for every
$h:Z\times A\to B$ there is exactly one map
$\lambda h:Z\to B^A$ satisfying
\[
 \operatorname{ev}\circ((\lambda h)\times1_A)=h.
\]
Here $(\lambda h)\times1_A$ is the product map formed by pairing
$(\lambda h)\circ\pi_Z$ with $\pi_A$.

title: Pullback
label: def:pullback-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
For arrows $a:X\to L$ and $b:Y\to L$, a \term{pullback} is an
object $P$ with maps $p_X:P\to X$, $p_Y:P\to Y$ satisfying
$a\circ p_X=b\circ p_Y$. For every $u:Z\to X$ and $v:Z\to Y$
with $a\circ u=b\circ v$, there is exactly one $w:Z\to P$ such that
$p_X\circ w=u$ and $p_Y\circ w=v$.

title: Pushout
label: def:pushout-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
For arrows $i:K\to A$ and $j:K\to B$, a \term{pushout} is an
object $J$ with maps $i_A:A\to J$, $i_B:B\to J$ satisfying
$i_A\circ i=i_B\circ j$, such that for every $a:A\to Z$ and $b:B\to Z$
with $a\circ i=b\circ j$ there is exactly one $u:J\to Z$ with
$u\circ i_A=a$ and $u\circ i_B=b$.

title: Adjunction
label: def:adjunction-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
Functors $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$
form an \term{adjunction}, written $F\dashv G$, when there is a
bijection
\[
 \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F(A),B)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(A,G(B))
\]
for all objects $A$ of $\mathcal C$ and $B$ of $\mathcal D$, natural in
both: composing with an arrow of $\mathcal C$ or of $\mathcal D$ before
or after the bijection gives the same result. $F$ is the
\term{left adjoint} and $G$ the \term{right adjoint}.

title: Adjoints of reindexing
label: prop:adjoints-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
In the set interpretation, $\Sigma_f\dashv f^*\dashv\Pi_f$: for every
family $E$ over $J$ and $B$ over $I$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathrm{Hom}(\Sigma_fE,B)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(E,f^*B),\\
 \mathrm{Hom}(f^*B,E)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(B,\Pi_fE),
 \end{gathered}
\]
naturally in $E$ and $B$.

title: Subobject classifier and topos
label: def:topos-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
An arrow $m:S\to X$ is a \term{monomorphism} when $m\circ u=m\circ v$
implies $u=v$ for all $u,v:Z\to S$; two monomorphisms into $X$ that
factor through each other by an isomorphism present the same
\term{subobject} of $X$. A \term{subobject classifier} is an object
$\Omega$ with an arrow $\mathrm{true}:1\to\Omega$ such that every
subobject $m:S\to X$ is the pullback of $\mathrm{true}$ along exactly one
arrow $\chi_m:X\to\Omega$, its \term{characteristic arrow}. A
topos is a category with a terminal object, pullbacks, exponentials and
a subobject classifier.

title: Sets form a topos
label: prop:finset-topos-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
$\mathsf{FinSet}$ and $\mathsf{Set}$ are topoi, with
$\Omega=\{0,1\}$ and $\mathrm{true}(*)=1$.

title: The Artform category is not a topos
label: prop:artform-not-topos-book
section: Category Caf\'e: a categorical view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
$\mathsf{Art}^{\mathrm{syn}}$ is a topos only when it has one frame and
no operation.

title: The laws of a rod
label: prop:rod-laws
section: Rules of inference: a type-theoretic view of artform \texorpdfstring{\mbox{calculus}~\optionalmark}{calculus}
statement:
For every rod $X$ the order on $\cells(X)$ is a linear order: no cell comes
before itself; if $a$ comes before $b$ and $b$ before $c$, then $a$ comes
before $c$; and of two different cells one comes before the other.

title: Stage frame
label: def:stage
statement:
The stage $\mathcal K_2$ is $\SquareGrid(5,5)$ together with the palette
that names its centre, orbit sites and gates, and the orientation of the
ring. For $n\ge2$ the stage $\mathcal K_n$ has a centre, $2n$ orbit sites
$v_0,\ldots,v_{2n-1}$ forming a ring, a gate on each orbit site, a spoke from
every orbit site to the centre, and the orientation $v_i\to v_{i+1}$, indices
taken modulo $2n$. Only $n=2$ is a marking of a square grid. For larger $n$
the ring is declared rather than read off a canvas.

title: Legal duet state
label: def:legal-state

title: Contract
label: def:contract
statement:
A \term{contract} for a stretch of a performance between two checkpoints
states what must hold at its first checkpoint, what it guarantees at its
last, and an \emph{invariant}, a condition on states that it keeps at every
checkpoint in between. Two
contracts \term[composition of contracts]{compose} when the guarantee of the
first gives what the second requires at their shared checkpoint.

title: Symmetry of a dance
label: def:dance-symmetry
statement:
A \term[symmetry of a dance]{symmetry} of a dance is a script $r$ on its
states that carries legal states to legal states and commutes with the
change $F_j$ that each count $j$ makes:
\[
r\cdot F_j(x)=F_j(r\cdot x)\qquad\text{for every count $j$ and every legal
state }x.
\]

title: Process profile; enabled application
label: def:process-profile
statement:
A \term{process profile} $p$ is one kind of change. It has a \term{guard}
$G_p$, the condition under which it may act; a \term{read footprint} $R_p$,
the cells it may look at; a \term{write footprint} $W_p$, the cells it may
change; and an \term{update proposal} $u_p$, the values it computes for its
write footprint from what it reads. It is \term{enabled} at a state $x$ when
$G_p(x)$ holds, and an \term{enabled application} of $p$ at $x$ is the
evidence that $G_p(x)$ holds together with the proposal $u_p$.

title: Compatibility; batch
label: def:batch
statement:
Two enabled applications are \term{compatible} when their writes do not
conflict and neither write invalidates a value that the other proposal
assumed. A \term{batch} is a finite family of pairwise compatible enabled
applications together with the evidence of their compatibility: the changes
that may be made one after another, in any order.

title: Slots, phases and checkpoints
label: def:slots-phases
section: The music: tapestries over a common score
statement:
A performance is scheduled in \term[slot]{slots}, each an occasion for work
of one kind; a slot says nothing about its physical duration or about how
many operations it holds. Slot $t$ of $N$ runs from
\term[boundary (of a slot)]{boundary} $t$ to boundary $t+1$, so the slot
support is $T=\LinearTime(N)$ and the boundary support is
$I=\LinearTime(N+1)$. The \term[phase (of a slot)]{phase} of a slot is the
kind of work it opens, read from a pointed clock over the slots. A
\term{checkpoint} is a boundary at which the state is read and declared
conditions must hold; an order-preserving selection $b$ of boundaries fixes
the checkpoints.

title: Control tapestry
label: def:control-tapestry
section: The music: tapestries over a common score
statement:
A \term{control tapestry} is a rectangular tapestry over the slot support
whose rows prescribe, slot by slot, the phase that is open and other control
values, such as cues, that rules may read. It says when each kind of work is
eligible. It never says which eligible change is made.

title: Trajectory; trace
label: def:trajectory-trace
statement:
An \term{execution}, or \emph{run}, is a performance as the rules carry it
out: the changes made count by count from the opening state, with the states
they pass through. The \term{trajectory} of an execution is the sequence of
its states at the checkpoints: what the dance did. Its \term{trace} is a
retained record of selected events: which rules were applied, at which
count, and in what order when the order is requested. Where waiting must
stay recoverable, the trace also keeps boundary records. The trace says how
the dance was made.

title: Finite cellular canvas
label: def:canvas
statement:
A finite $d$-dimensional \term{canvas} $X$ is a finite form carrying graded
cell sets $C_k(X)$ for $0\le k\le d$, an immediate-face relation $a\lessdot b$
raising dimension by exactly one, and a face-closed outer boundary $\partial X$.
The local boundary data used for its cells are supplied as in
\cref{def:finite-cell-pattern}. For polygonal faces this includes a closed
boundary cycle; an orientation, when selected, chooses its traversal direction.
Its positions are the graded disjoint sum
\[
 \pos(X)=\coprod_{k=0}^{d}C_k(X)
   \cong\AFDepPair_{k:\{0,\ldots,d\}}C_k(X).
\]

title: Position presentation
label: def:position-presentation
statement:
A \term{position presentation} of a form $F$ is a finite set $\pos(F)$
together with a typed map
\[
\pi_F:\pos(F)\longrightarrow\cells(F)
\]
naming, for each visible address, the carried cell it presents.

title: Cube boundary assembled from squares
label: prop:cube-assembly-book
section: Shapes, parts, and how pieces make a whole
statement:
Six square instances with the coordinate-face gluing data above
assemble to an instance of $\mathsf{CubeBoundary}$. Adding the
declared cubical three-cell along its whole boundary gives an
instance of $\mathsf{Cube}$ with cell counts $(8,12,6,1)$.

title: Geometric part and construction records
label: def:geometric-records-book
section: Shapes, parts, and how pieces make a whole
statement:
Fix a common geometric comparison profile $\sigma$ for parts and
target. A \term{part family} $\mathsf{PartFamily}_\sigma(X)$ consists
of a finite index set $I$, actual part canvases $X_i$ with declared
shape types, and structural embeddings $j_i:U_\sigma X_i\hookrightarrow
U_\sigma X$.

An \term{assembly record} $D:\mathsf{AssemblyData}_\sigma((X_i))$
specifies interface canvases and their maps into pieces, the
identifications they generate, and evidence that the quotient is
admitted in the selected incidence/local-boundary vocabulary. Its
result contains the joined canvas $Q_D$, the maps from the pieces,
and their compatibility. Any chosen outer-boundary mark is additional
output data.

A \term{decomposition} $\delta:\mathsf{Decomposition}_\sigma(X)$ retains
such a part family and assembly record, together with a structural
isomorphism
$\theta:Q_D\cong U_\sigma X$ identifying the piece maps with $j_i$.
Here $Q_D$ assembles the part reducts $U_\sigma X_i$, so the result
and target are compared in the same vocabulary.

title: Recognition profile
label: def:recognition-profile
statement:
A \term{recognition profile} $\AFRecognitionProfile$ selects what a match may see: a finite
family of \term{sorts} of position, that is, of types of position in the
sense of \cref{sec:types-values}, which a match must preserve; the relations
among positions that the match reads; the finite-valued labels and state channels it reads; and any
allowed action on directional or palette labels.

title: Recognition pattern
label: def:recognition-pattern-book
statement:
A \term{recognition pattern} under $\AFRecognitionProfile$ is a finite
template with all observations and state data selected by that profile,
satisfying their declared legality conditions. Write
$P:\RecognitionPattern(\AFRecognitionProfile)$ for this typed package.

title: Strong occurrence
label: def:strong-occurrence
statement:
A \term{strong occurrence} $w:P\hookrightarrow X$ under $\AFRecognitionProfile$, also read as a
strong match, is an injective sort-preserving map of positions such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item all selected relations are preserved;
\item those relations are reflected on the image; and
\item selected labels and channel values agree through the declared label
map.
\end{enumerate}
On a cellular canvas the sorts are the dimensions, so $w$ is an injective
dimension-preserving cell map that preserves and reflects the selected
incidence and orientation relations and agrees on palette labels. The type of
such witnesses is $\Occurrence_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(P,X)$.

title: Positive reduct, positive template, positive instantiation
label: def:positive-feature-template-book
statement:
Let $G$ be a state profiled by $\AFRecognitionProfile$. Its \term{positive reduct}
$\AtP_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(G)$ is the finite set of \term{atoms} true in $G$: one atom
$R(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$ for each selected relation $R$ and each tuple of
positions on which it holds, and one atom $[a=v](x_1,\ldots,x_k)$ for each
selected finite-valued channel $a$ and each tuple at which it takes the value
$v$. Sorts are types of position and are not atoms.

A \term{positive template} $K=(E_K,\mathcal A_K)$ is a finite sorted set of
variables $E_K$ together with a nonempty finite set $\mathcal A_K$ of atoms
over them, every variable occurring in at least one atom. A \term{positive
instantiation} of $K$ in $G$ is a sort-preserving injection
$j:E_K\hookrightarrow\pos(G)$ with
\[
j_*(\mathcal A_K)\subseteq\AtP_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(G),
\]
where $j_*$ renames the variables of each atom by $j$. The type of such
witnesses is $\Instantiation_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K,G)$.

title: Partial positive comparison
label: def:partial-positive-comparison
statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be states profiled by $\AFRecognitionProfile$. A \term{partial positive
comparison} $F:G_1\rightharpoonup G_2$ is a sort-preserving injection from a
subset $D\subseteq\pos(G_1)$, its domain, into $\pos(G_2)$. An atom of
$\AtP_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(G_1)$ whose positions all lie in $D$ is \term{credited} to $F$ when
its image under $F$ is an atom of $\AtP_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(G_2)$. The credited atoms form
the set $\Pres^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(F)$, and the positions occurring in them are the
\term{active} positions of $F$.

title: Shared positive pattern
label: prop:shared-positive-pattern-book
statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be states profiled by $\AFRecognitionProfile$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If a positive template $K$ has an instantiation $j_1$ in $G_1$ and an
instantiation $j_2$ in $G_2$, then $F=j_2\circ j_1^{-1}$, defined on
$j_1(E_K)$, is a partial positive comparison $G_1\rightharpoonup G_2$, and
every atom of $j_{1*}(\mathcal A_K)$ is credited to it.
\item If a partial positive comparison $F:G_1\rightharpoonup G_2$ credits at
least one atom, then renaming its active positions to fresh variables and
transporting its credited atoms gives a positive template $K_F$, with an
instantiation $j_1$ in $G_1$ by the renaming and an instantiation
$j_2=F\circ j_1$ in $G_2$; and $j_2\circ j_1^{-1}$ is $F$ restricted to the
active positions.
\end{enumerate}

title: Partial profile isomorphism
label: prop:partial-profile-iso-book
statement:
Let $F:D\to D'$ be a sort-preserving bijection between a set of positions of
$G_1$ and a set of positions of $G_2$, and let every selected relation and
channel be total on both sides, so that every well-sorted tuple of $D$ and
of $D'$ has a verdict or a value. If the selected tables of $G_1$ on $D$ and
of $G_2$ on $D'$ agree through $F$ in both directions, then $F$ is a strong
occurrence of the restriction of $G_1$ to $D$ in $G_2$ and $F^{-1}$ is one in
the other direction. Such an $F$ is a \term{partial profile isomorphism}.
Equivalently, $F$ and $F^{-1}$ each credit every atom of their domain.

title: Group
label: def:group
statement:
A \term{group} is a set $G$ with an operation $G\times G\to G$, written
$(g,h)\mapsto gh$, such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=.15em]
\item the operation is associative, $(gh)k=g(hk)$;
\item some element $1\in G$ satisfies $1g=g1=g$ for every $g$;
\item every $g$ has an inverse $g^{-1}$ with $gg^{-1}=g^{-1}g=1$.
\end{enumerate}
The \term{order} of $G$, written $|G|$, is the number of its elements; this
book's groups are finite unless \cref{sec:group-table} says otherwise. A
\term{subgroup} is a subset containing $1$ and closed under the operation and
under inverses; we write $H\le G$.

title: Abelian
label: def:abelian
statement:
A group is \term{abelian} when $gh=hg$ for every $g$ and $h$, and
\term[non-abelian]{non-abelian} otherwise.

title: Cyclic group
label: def:cyclic-group
statement:
A group is \term{cyclic} when some single element $g$ generates it, meaning
every element is a power $g^k$. The cyclic group of order $n$ is written
$C_n$; it is $\{1,g,g^2,\ldots,g^{n-1}\}$ with $g^n=1$.

title: Dihedral group
label: def:dihedral-group
statement:
The \term{dihedral group} $D_n$ is the symmetry group of a regular $n$-gon:
its $n$ rotations together with its $n$ reflections, so
\[
|D_n|=2n .
\]
Its rotations form the cyclic subgroup $C_n\le D_n$. It has half
the elements of $D_n$: the other half are reflections.

title: Homomorphism, kernel, isomorphism
label: def:homomorphism
statement:
A \term{homomorphism} $\varphi:G\to H$ satisfies
$\varphi(gh)=\varphi(g)\varphi(h)$. Its \term{kernel} is
$\ker\varphi=\{g\mid\varphi(g)=1\}$, a subgroup of $G$; it measures what
$\varphi$ forgets. A bijective homomorphism is an \term{isomorphism}, written
$G\cong H$, and its existence is a \role{WITNESS} that the two groups differ
only in the names of their elements.

title: Conjugacy class
label: def:conjugacy
statement:
Elements $g$ and $aga^{-1}$ are \term{conjugate}. Conjugacy is an equivalence
relation, and its classes partition $G$. For each fixed $a$, the map
$g\mapsto aga^{-1}$ is an invertible \role{SCRIPT} on $G$; the classes are what
every such script preserves.

title: Continuous groups named in this book
label: def:continuous-groups
section: Which groups, and how many kinds
statement:
The \term{circle group} $U(1)$ is the complex numbers of modulus one under
multiplication. $SO(3)$ is the group of rotations of three-dimensional space;
$SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ are the groups of $2\times2$ and $3\times3$ complex
matrices that are unitary and have determinant one. Each has infinitely many
elements, described by continuously varying parameters --- one angle for
$U(1)$, three for $SO(3)$ and $SU(2)$, eight for $SU(3)$.

title: Automorphism group
label: def:automorphism-group
statement:
For a pattern $X$ and profile $\AFRecognitionProfile$, the \term{automorphism group}
$\Aut_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(X)$ is the group of invertible members of $\Occurrence_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(X,X)$.

title: Template symmetry, atom image, positive occurrence
label: def:positive-occurrence-book
statement:
For a positive template $K=(E_K,\mathcal A_K)$ the \term{positive
automorphism group} $\Aut^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K)$ is the group of sort-preserving
bijections $a:E_K\to E_K$ with $a_*(\mathcal A_K)=\mathcal A_K$. It acts on
$\Instantiation_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K,G)$ by precomposition, $j\mapsto j\circ a$. The
\term{atom image} of an instantiation is
\[
\aim_K(j)=j_*(\mathcal A_K)\subseteq\AtP_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(G),
\]
the set of atoms of $G$ it instantiates. A \term{positive occurrence} of $K$
in $G$ is an orbit of this action, and the set of occurrences is
\[
\Occurrence^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K,G)=\Instantiation_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K,G)\big/\Aut^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K).
\]

title: Positive occurrences are atom images
label: prop:atom-image-occurrence-book
statement:
The action of $\Aut^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K)$ on $\Instantiation_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K,G)$ is free, and two
instantiations have the same atom image if and only if they differ by an
element of $\Aut^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K)$, which is then unique. Hence
$[j]\mapsto\aim_K(j)$ is a bijection from $\Occurrence^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K,G)$ onto the
set of instantiated atom sets in $G$.

title: Component inventory and degree
label: def:pattern-degree-book
statement:
Call two credited atoms of a partial positive comparison $F$ adjacent when
they share a position, and call a class of the resulting connectedness
relation, together with the positions occurring in its atoms, an
\term{atom-sharing component}. The \term{component inventory} of $F$ is the
list of pairs $(o_C,p_C)$, one per component $C$, of its numbers of positions
and of atoms. The \term{degree} of $F$ is the readout
\[
\deg(F)=\sum_C o_C\,p_C .
\]
For a positive template the same definitions apply to its own atoms and
variables.

title: Atom support and atom-disjoint recurrence
label: def:atom-disjoint-recurrence-book
statement:
The \term{atom support} of a positive occurrence is its atom image, which
\cref{prop:atom-image-occurrence-book} makes independent of the
representative. Two occurrences are \term{atom-disjoint} when their supports
are disjoint; they may share positions. A template $K$ \term{recurs
internally} in $G$ when $\Occurrence^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K,G)$ contains two atom-disjoint
members, and \term{recurs externally} when it has one occurrence in $G$ and
one in a state of a declared reference repertoire. The recurrence witness is
a family of pairwise atom-disjoint occurrences of maximum size, retained
together with the claim.

title: Averaged invariant metric
label: thm:averaged-invariant-metric
statement:
The averaged form $\angles{-,-}_G$ is a positive-definite inner product and is
$G$-invariant: $\angles{h u,h v}_G=\angles{u,v}_G$ for every $h\in G$.

title: Perpendicularity from symmetry
label: prop:perpendicularity-from-symmetry
statement:
For a $G$-invariant inner product, the $+1$ and $-1$ eigenspaces of a
reflection are perpendicular.

title: Commuting compatible changes
label: prop:commuting-proposals
section: Finite ambient schemes and located patches
statement:
If two enabled applications are compatible, making one and then the other
gives the same state in either order.

title: Policy
label: def:policy
section: Finite ambient schemes and located patches
statement:
A \term{policy} is a complete assignment in the sense of
\cref{sec:complete-assignment} that gives each state of a run, together with
any memory of its own, one batch of the applications enabled there, possibly
empty. It is the only thing in a run that chooses: the rules say which
applications are enabled, and the policy says which are made.

title: Stabilization
label: thm:growth-stabilization
statement:
If $W$ has finitely many cells and $F_W$ is extensive, then the increasing
sequence $X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots$ stabilizes after finitely many
strict growth steps.

title: Cadence fairness; application fairness
label: def:fairness
statement:
A continuing execution is \term[cadence fairness]{cadence fair} when its
control tapestry keeps opening every phase that pending work needs. It is
\term[application fairness]{application fair} when its policy eventually
selects every application that stays enabled each time its phase is open.

title: Bounded windowed progress
label: def:windowed-progress
statement:
Let $b,c$ be positive integers and $k$ a nonnegative integer. An execution
makes \emph{bounded windowed progress} with these constants when, for every
pending application whose guard stays valid, the next offer and each later
offer arrive within $c$ steps, the application is served by its $b$th
offer, and once served it is made within a further $k$ steps.

title: Fair closure
label: prop:fair-closure
statement:
In a fixed finite window of possible cells, every run that meets these
three hypotheses reaches the least closed patch above its seed and stays
there.

title: Symmetry of growth
label: prop:growth-symmetry
statement:
Let a positive attachment rule be carried to itself by a group $G$ of motions
of the canvas, and let the motions of a subgroup $S$ fix the seed.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $n$, the set of patches that some run reaches in $n$ steps
  is carried to itself by every motion of $S$.
\item The policy that makes every enabled attachment at once keeps the
  symmetry $S$ at every step.
\item At a patch that $S$ fixes, a policy that makes one attachment keeps
  $S$ only if the attached face is fixed by every motion of $S$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Sigma-algebra
label: def:sigma-algebra
section: The measurable space a canvas carries
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a set. A \term{sigma-algebra} $\mathcal A$ on $\Omega$ is a
collection of subsets such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $\Omega\in\mathcal A$;
\item if $A\in\mathcal A$, then $\Omega\setminus A\in\mathcal A$; and
\item if $A_1,A_2,\ldots\in\mathcal A$, then
$\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\in\mathcal A$.
\end{enumerate}
The pair $(\Omega,\mathcal A)$ is a \term{measurable space}.

title: Measure
label: def:measure
section: The measurable space a canvas carries
statement:
A \term{measure} on $(\Omega,\mathcal A)$ is a function
$\mu:\mathcal A\to[0,\infty]$ such that $\mu(\varnothing)=0$ and for every
pairwise disjoint sequence $(A_n)$,
\[
\mu\left(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\right)=
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).
\]
The triple $(\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)$ is a \term{measure space}.

title: Measurable map
label: def:measurable-map
section: Measurable maps, pushforward, and product measure
statement:
A function $f:(\Omega,\mathcal A)\to(Y,\mathcal B)$ is \term{measurable} if
$f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal A$ for every $B\in\mathcal B$.

title: Finite Fubini--Tonelli
label: prop:finite-fubini-tonelli
section: Measurable maps, pushforward, and product measure
statement:
For a nonnegative function $h:X\times Y\to[0,\infty]$ on finite spaces,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{x,y}h(x,y)w_xv_y
 &=\sum_xw_x\left(\sum_yh(x,y)v_y\right)\\
 &=\sum_yv_y\left(\sum_xh(x,y)w_x\right).
\end{align*}
For real-valued $h$, the same holds whenever the finite weighted sum of
$|h|$ is finite.

title: Measurability
label: def:measurability
statement:
A function between measurable spaces,
\[
f:(\Omega,\mathcal A)\longrightarrow(\R,\mathcal B(\R)),
\]
is measurable when
$f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal A$ for every Borel set $B\subseteq\R$. On a finite
power-set space, every real-valued function is measurable.

title: Monotone convergence
label: thm:monotone-convergence
statement:
If $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$ are measurable and
$f_n(x)\to f(x)$, then
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\dd\mu=\int f\dd\mu.
\]

label: prop:invariant-measure-orbits
statement: An invariant atomic measure is constant on each $G$-orbit.

title: Weighted cellular content
label: def:weighted-cellular-content
statement:
Fix a dimension $d$ and a weight $w_T\ge0$ for each allowed $d$-cell type
$T$. For a finite cellular region $X$, define
\[
\Cont_d(X)=\sum_{c\in X_d}w_{\mathrm{type}(c)}.
\]
Here $X_d$ is the set of its $d$-cell identities.

title: Receipts decide, and margins protect
label: prop:metric-feature-receipts-book
statement:
Each receipt above is decided by finitely many comparisons of rational
numbers, so every accepted receipt is an exact finite verdict. Let a second
sampled picture be supplied with bijections of the parts and of their pixel
regions that preserve pixel adjacency, boundaries, joint sites and the
complete candidate inventories, and let every inequality of every receipt
change by less than its recorded margin. Then every verdict is preserved and
the two observations produce the same feature state.

title: Reference marking along a comparison
label: prop:reference-marking-pullback-book
statement:
Let $j_s$ and $j_v$ instantiate $K$ in $G_s$ and $G_v$, let
$F=j_v\circ j_s^{-1}$, and let $\lambda_v$ be a marking of $j_v(E_K)$. Then
$\lambda_v\circ F$ is a marking of $j_s(E_K)$, and replacing $j_s$ by
$j_s\circ a$ for $a\in\Aut^{+}_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(K)$ replaces it by
$\lambda_v\circ j_v\circ a^{-1}\circ j_s^{-1}$. The pulled-back marking is
indexed by the comparison, and it is unchanged under $a$ only when
$\lambda_v\circ j_v$ is.

title: Events available to a finite report
label: def:report-events
statement:
For a map $f:\Omega\to Y$ between finite sets, the report event algebra
on the source is $\mathcal A_f=\{f^{-1}(C):C\subseteq Y\}$.
Its nonempty atoms are the nonempty fibers $f^{-1}(\{y\})$.
An event is available to this report precisely when it is a union of
these fibers.

title: Counting retained alternatives
label: probbook:count-law
statement:
For a finite nonempty set $\Omega$ of equal-weight retained alternatives,
a finite set $Y$, and a report map $f:\Omega\to Y$, normalized counting pushes forward to
\[
 P_Y(C)=\frac{|f^{-1}(C)|}{|\Omega|},\qquad C\subseteq Y.
\]
This is a probability measure on the finite power set of $Y$.

title: Conditioning on a positive-mass event
label: def:conditioning
section: Changing the report; conditioning on a record
statement:
If $E$ is measurable and $P(E)>0$, the conditional probability of $A$
given $E$ is
\[
 P(A\mid E)=\frac{P(A\cap E)}{P(E)}.
\]
It is the normalized restriction of the original measure to $E$.

title: Exit-level closure
label: prob:markov
section: Why records and fresh preparations matter
statement:
Suppose that, conditional on every positive-probability complete past,
the next response pair is uniform on $B\times B$. Suppose the next exit
is $x\oplus ab$, with no further dependence on that past, and later
updates preserve the previous exit records. Then the recorded exit
process has conditional transition law $K(y\mid x)$ from
\cref{prob:controller}. Its next-exit law given its recorded history
depends only on its current exit.

title: Extension of compatible finite histories
label: probbook:history-extension
statement:
Suppose normalized nonnegative laws $P_n$ on the first $n$ report
alphabets satisfy
$\sum_{y\in Y_{n+1}}P_{n+1}(h,y)=P_n(h)$.
There is exactly one probability measure on
$(\Omega_\infty,\mathcal A_\infty)$ assigning mass $P_n(h)$ to $[h]$.

title: Deterministic law; tick; run
label: def:tick
statement:
Let $A$ be a frame (\cref{def:frame-instance}). A \term{deterministic law} on
$A$ gives each state of $A$ the state that follows it. The map $F$ that does
so is the law's \term{tick}, or tick map, and the \term{run} of the law from a
state $x$
is the sequence $x,F(x),F(F(x)),\ldots$, one state at every tick.

title: Local law; halo
label: def:local-law
statement:
A deterministic law on a canvas $X$ is \term{local} when the new value at
each cell depends only on the old values at the cells within a fixed number
of edges of it, the cell's \term{halo}.

title: Symmetry of a law; conserved reading
label: def:law-symmetry
statement:
Let a deterministic law have tick $F$. A \term[symmetry of a
law]{symmetry} of the law is a script $s$ on its states that commutes with
the tick:
\[
F(s(x))=s(F(x))\qquad\text{for every state }x.
\]
A reading $q$ of the states is \term[conserved reading]{conserved} by the law
when $q(F(x))=q(x)$ for every state $x$.

title: What a conserved reading can see
label: thm:orbit-criterion
statement:
Let the tick $F$ of a deterministic law be a bijection of its finite set of states, so
that the states fall into orbits $\{x,F(x),F^2(x),\ldots\}$
(\cref{sec:clock-trajectory}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item A reading is conserved exactly when it is constant on each orbit.
\item A symmetry $s$ carries every orbit onto an orbit. Some conserved reading
  tells $x$ from $s(x)$, for some $x$, exactly when $s$ carries some orbit onto
  a different orbit.
\end{enumerate}

title: Affine law; tally; pairing
label: def:affine-law
statement:
Let the states of a deterministic law be the tables on a finite set of cells with values in
$\Zmod{n}$, added cell by cell. The law is \term[affine law]{affine} when its
tick has the form $F(p)=M(p)+b$, where $M$ is a bijection with
$M(p+q)=M(p)+M(q)$ and $b$ is a fixed table, the \term{source}. A
\term{tally} is an additive reading: a reading $T$ with values in $\Zmod{n}$ and
$T(p+q)=T(p)+T(q)$. A \term{pairing} is a rule $\langle p,q\rangle$ that is a
tally in each argument. It is \term[perfect pairing]{perfect} when every tally is
$\langle w,\cdot\rangle$ for exactly one table $w$, and the law
\term[keeping a pairing]{keeps} it when
$\langle M(p),M(q)\rangle=\langle p,q\rangle$ for all tables $p,q$.

title: Noether's theorem for affine laws
label: thm:noether
statement:
Let an affine law $F(p)=M(p)+b$ keep a pairing $\langle\,,\rangle$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every table $w$ with $M(w)=w$, adding $w$ to every state is a
  symmetry of the law, and the tally $T_w(p)=\langle w,p\rangle$ changes at
  every tick by exactly the source's share:
  \[
  T_w(F(p))=T_w(p)+\langle w,b\rangle .
  \]
  In particular $T_w$ is conserved when $\langle w,b\rangle=0$.
\item If the pairing is perfect, every conserved tally is $T_w$ for exactly
  one table $w$, and that $w$ has $M(w)=w$ and $\langle w,b\rangle=0$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Noether's theorem on the square
label: cor:noether-square
statement:
For the law of the square and the pairing
$\langle p,q\rangle=\sum_ip(v_i)q(v_i)$, the tables fixed by the tick are the
three constant ones; adding the same number at every corner is a symmetry;
the tally paired with adding $1$ at every corner is the total
$T(p)=p(v_0)+p(v_1)+p(v_2)+p(v_3)$ modulo $3$, and it is conserved; and every
conserved tally is $0$, $T$ or $2T$.

title: The current of a tally
label: prop:tally-current
statement:
Let an affine law $F(p)=M(p)+b$ keep the tally $T(p)=\sum_vd(v)\,p(v)$. For
cells $u\ne v$ put
\[
J_{u\to v}(p)=d(v)\,M_{vu}\,p(u).
\]
Then at every tick and every cell $v$
\[
d(v)\bigl(F(p)(v)-p(v)\bigr)=\sum_{u\ne v}J_{u\to v}(p)-\sum_{y\ne v}J_{v\to y}(p)+d(v)\,b(v),
\]
and the source terms $d(v)\,b(v)$ add up to $0$. The current runs from $u$ to
$v$ only if the update of $v$ reads $u$, and it reads the cell $u$ alone.

title: Law; move; legal state
label: def:law
statement:
Let $A$ be a frame (\cref{def:frame-instance}). A \term{law} on $A$ declares
finitely many conditions on the tables of $A$, its \term{invariants}; the
tables that satisfy every invariant are its \term[legal state]{legal states}.
At each legal state the law lists finitely many \term{moves}: the changes it
allows there, each leading to a legal state. A law says which moves are
allowed. It does not say which of them is made.

title: Realizer; run
label: def:realizer
statement:
A \term[realizer!of a law]{realizer} of a law $L$ is a policy together with
evidence that every batch it selects keeps the invariants of $L$. The policy
is of one of three kinds: \emph{deterministic}, one batch at every legal
state; \emph{relational}, a declared set of allowed batches there; or
\emph{stochastic}, weights on the allowed batches. A \term{run} from a legal
start over a finite line of ticks $\mathcal T$ is a trajectory of legal states
in which every step applies a batch the realizer selects (for a relational
realizer, one it allows; for a stochastic one, one of positive weight),
together with the trace of the moves made.

title: The law decides what is kept
label: prop:law-decides
statement:
If every batch a law allows carries states satisfying an invariant to states
satisfying it, then every run keeps the invariant: the run of a deterministic
realizer, each run a relational realizer allows, and each run of positive
weight under a stochastic one.

title: Law in steps; score; checkpoint; well-posed realizer
label: def:law-steps
statement:
A \term{law in steps} is a law (\cref{def:law}) whose moves each belong to one
of finitely many \term{steps}, together with a \term{score}: a control tapestry
(\cref{def:control-tapestry}) whose row says, slot by slot, which step is
open. Only the moves of the open step are enabled, and one pass through the
repeating pattern of the score is a tick. Each invariant comes with the slots
at whose close it must hold, its \term{checkpoints} (\cref{def:slots-phases}).
A deterministic realizer of a law in steps is
\term[well posed]{well posed} when it is \emph{total}, selecting a nonempty
batch at every legal state and open step except where the score allows an
empty one, and \emph{order-free}: applying the moves of a selected batch in
any order gives the same state.

title: Finite well-posedness
label: thm:well-posed
statement:
Let a law in steps have a well-posed deterministic realizer. From every legal
start, over every finite stretch of the score, the realizer has exactly one
run. The order in which the moves of each batch are applied does not change
its states, and every invariant holds at each of its checkpoints.

title: Five kinds of equation
label: def:equation-roles
section: What kind of statement is\\ an equation?

title: Right torsor
label: def:torsor
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. A \term{right $G$-torsor} is a nonempty finite set
$T$ with a right action $(x,g)\mapsto x\cdot g$ that is
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=.1em]
\item \term{free}: $x\cdot g=x$ forces $g=1$; and
\item \term{transitive}: for all $x,y\in T$ there is $g$ with $x\cdot g=y$.
\end{enumerate}
Write $\Torsor(G)$ for the type of right $G$-torsors.

title: Pose orbit
label: lem:pose-torsor
statement:
Let $G=\Aut_{\AFRecognitionProfile}(P)$ act on marked data $m$ carried by a recognition pattern $P$, and
suppose the mark is \term{rigid}, meaning $\Stab_G(m)=1$: no symmetry but
the identity leaves the mark where it was. Then the orbit
\[
\PoseOrbit(P,m)=\{g\cdot m\mid g\in G\}
\]
is a right $G$-torsor under $(g\cdot m)\cdot k:=(gk)\cdot m$. For the marked
octagon and its rotations, $G=C_8$, $m$ is the marked corner, and the orbit is
the eight poses.

title: Localization
label: def:localization
statement:
Let $K:\CellForm$ be a canvas and $G$ a finite group. A \term{localization} is
a choice of one torsor at each vertex,
\[
\mathcal T=(T_v)_{v}:\Localize(K,G)
:=\AFDepFun_{v: C_0(K)}\Torsor(G).
\]
The torsor $T_v$ is the \term[fibre!of a localization]{fibre} of
$\mathcal T$ over $v$.

title: Connection
label: def:connection-general
statement:
Let $\mathcal T=(T_v)_v:\Localize(K,G)$. An \term{equivariant map} of right
$G$-torsors is a bijection $\sigma:T\to T'$ with
$\sigma(x\cdot g)=\sigma(x)\cdot g$. A
\term{connection} on $\mathcal T$ is a family
\[
\mathcal U=(\mathcal U_e)_{e\in E^{\mathrm{or}}(K)},
\qquad
\mathcal U_e:T_{s(e)}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }T_{t(e)}\ \text{equivariant},
\]
one for each oriented edge of the transport skeleton, subject to the reversal
law $\mathcal U_{\bar e}=\mathcal U_e^{-1}$. Write $\Connection(K;G)$ for the
type of such families.

title: Trivialization and link table
label: def:trivialization
statement:
A \term{trivialization} is a choice of origin $t_v\in T_v$ at every vertex.
Given one, freeness and transitivity supply for each oriented edge a
\emph{unique} group element $U_e$ with
\begin{equation}
\mathcal U_e(t_{s(e)})=t_{t(e)}\cdot U_e .

\end{equation}
Here $t_{s(e)}$ and $t_{t(e)}$ are the origins at the source $s(e)$ and the
target $t(e)$ of $e$. The table $U=(U_e)_e$ is the \term{link table} of $\mathcal U$ in that
trivialization, and it inhabits
\[
\LinkTable(K,G)=\bigl\{(U_e)_e\mid U_e\in G,\ U_{\bar e}=U_e^{-1}\bigr\}.
\]

title: Connection and coordinates
label: prop:connection-coordinates
statement:
Fix a localization $\mathcal T$ and a trivialization $t=(t_v)_v$. Then
\eqref{eq:link-coordinate} defines a bijection
\[
\Phi_t:\Connection(K;G)\longrightarrow\LinkTable(K,G).
\]

title: Gauge group and gauge orbit
label: def:gauge-group
statement:
The equivariant bijections $T_v\to T_v$ form a group, $\Aut_G(T_v)$. Given an
origin $t_v$, each $\alpha_v$ in it is fixed by one group element $h_v$, the
one with $\alpha_v(t_v)=t_v\cdot h_v$, since equivariance then gives
$\alpha_v(t_v\cdot g)=t_v\cdot h_vg$ for every $g$. The \term{gauge group} of
the localization is the product over vertices,
\[
\mathcal G_K=\prod_{v\in C_0(K)}\Aut_G(T_v),
\]
which a trivialization identifies with $\prod_v G$. It acts on connections by
\begin{equation}
(\alpha\cdot\mathcal U)_e
=\alpha_{t(e)}\circ\mathcal U_e\circ\alpha_{s(e)}^{-1},

\end{equation}
and two connections in the same orbit are \term{gauge equivalent}. In
coordinates, \eqref{eq:active-gauge} is again
$U_e\mapsto h_{t(e)}U_eh_{s(e)}^{-1}$.

title: Holonomy descent
label: thm:holonomy-descent
section: Holonomy, and what survives a gauge change
statement:
Under the substitution \eqref{eq:gauge-action},
\begin{equation}
\Hol_{U^h}(\gamma)=h_{v_k}\,\Hol_U(\gamma)\,h_{v_0}^{-1}.

\end{equation}
In particular, for a loop based at $v_0$ the holonomy changes by conjugation,
so its conjugacy class is unchanged: the class \emph{descends} to gauge
orbits, which means that it takes one value on each orbit.

title: Class function and Wilson loop
label: def:wilson
section: Holonomy, and what survives a gauge change
statement:
A map $\kappa:G\to Y$ is a \term{class function} when
$\kappa(aga^{-1})=\kappa(g)$ for all $a,g$, so it depends only on the
conjugacy class of \cref{def:conjugacy}. For
a representation $\rho$ of $G$ --- a homomorphism into invertible matrices ---
the \term{character} $\chi_\rho(g)=\Tr\rho(g)$ is a class function, and
$\chi_\rho(\Hol_U(\gamma))$ on a loop is called a \term{Wilson loop}. On an
open path, $\rho(\Hol_U(\gamma))$ is called a \term{Wilson line}. These are
the standard names in lattice gauge theory, where the same objects are built
over a continuous group.

title: Face curvature
label: def:curvature-general
statement:
Let $f$ be an oriented face, let $v$ be a vertex on its declared boundary word,
and read that word as a loop $\partial_vf$ based at $v$. The \term{curvature}
of $f$ at $v$ is
\[
F^v_U(f)=\Hol_U(\partial_vf).
\]
A connection is \term{flat at $f$} when this is the identity, a condition that
does not depend on which boundary vertex was chosen.

title: Three kinds of triviality
label: def:flatness

title: Pure gauge equals loop-flat
label: thm:pure-gauge
statement:
On a connected transport skeleton, a connection is pure gauge if and only if
it is loop-flat.

title: Spanning-tree gauge fixing
label: thm:tree-gauge-fixing
statement:
Let the transport skeleton be finite and connected and let $\tau$ be a spanning
tree. Every link table is gauge equivalent to one with $U_e=1$ on every edge of
$\tau$. The gauge transformations preserving that normalization are exactly the
constant ones $h_v=k$, and they conjugate every remaining label by the same
$k$. Writing $E^+(K)$ for one orientation of each underlying edge,
\[
\LinkTable(K,G)/\mathcal G_K
\;\cong\;
G^{\,|E^+(K)|-|C_0(K)|+1}\big/G ,
\]
where the final $G$ acts by simultaneous conjugation.

title: Classification of face-flat connections
label: thm:flat-classification
statement:
Let the transport skeleton be connected. Define $\pi_1(K,v_*)$ combinatorially:
based edge loops at $v_*$, modulo deletion of immediate backtracks and
insertion or deletion of declared face-boundary words. Then holonomy induces a
bijection
\[
\{\text{face-flat connections}\}\big/\text{gauge}
\;\cong\;
\Hom\bigl(\pi_1(K,v_*),G\bigr)\big/G ,
\]
with $G$ acting by conjugating all values. The pure-gauge connections
correspond to the trivial homomorphism.

title: Matter field and covariant transport
label: def:matter
statement:
A \term{representation} of $G$, as in \cref{def:wilson}, is a homomorphism
$\rho:G\to GL(V)$ into the invertible linear maps of a finite-dimensional
complex vector space $V$. A \term{matter field} is
a table $\psi:C_0(K)\to V$, one vector $\psi_v$ at every vertex, and the
connection transports it \term{covariantly} along $e:u\to v$ by
\[
\psi_u\;\longmapsto\;\rho(U_e)\,\psi_u .
\]

title: Invariant vertex coupling
label: def:intertwiner
statement:
Let matter fields $\psi^{(1)},\ldots,\psi^{(m)}$ with representations
$\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_m$ on spaces $V_1,\ldots,V_m$ be carried into a vertex
$v$, the $k$th along an edge $e_k$ from $u_k$, so that the value
$w_k=\rho_k(U_{e_k})\psi^{(k)}_{u_k}$ arrives in $V_k$. An
\term{intertwiner} at $v$ is a function $\iota(w_1,\ldots,w_m)\in\C$, linear
in each argument, such that
\[
\iota\bigl(\rho_1(g)w_1,\ldots,\rho_m(g)w_m\bigr)=\iota(w_1,\ldots,w_m)
\]
for every $g\in G$ and all $w_k\in V_k$. Such a function is the same thing as
a linear map on the tensor product $V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_m$, the form in
which later chapters write it. A coupling built from an intertwiner is gauge
invariant; one built without is not, however natural it looks.

title: Gauss constraint
label: def:gauss
statement:
A \term{Gauss constraint} is a gauge-invariant predicate on the total state,
selecting which states are legal. An inhabitant of it at a particular state is
a \role{WITNESS}, evidence in the sense of \cref{sec:evidence-preview}, a value
of a type that may be empty; the constraint is not an evolution rule and does
not by itself move anything.

title: Gauge-safe profile
label: def:gauge-safe
statement:
A recognition profile $\AFRecognitionProfile$ on a gauge state type is \term{gauge-safe} when for
every state $x$ and every $\alpha\in\mathcal G_K$ the identity correspondence on
positions is an invertible $\AFRecognitionProfile$-match $x\to\alpha\cdot x$. Occurrence counts
of a gauge-safe profile then agree on gauge-equivalent states, so they descend
to the gauge orbit.

title: Gauge-covariant law and realizer
label: def:gauge-covariant-law
section: A law on a gauge frame
statement:
Let a law act on the states of a gauge frame: a connection, in link
coordinates, together with fields at the vertices and any further fields the
law declares. A gauge change $h$ acts on the links by \eqref{eq:gauge-action},
at each vertex $v$ by $h_v$ (a pose by $g_v\mapsto h_vg_v$, a matter value by
$\psi_v\mapsto\rho(h_v)\psi_v$), and on the further fields by a declared
action. The law is \term{gauge covariant} when two things hold for every
gauge change $h$ and every state $x$. First, each move enabled at $x$ is also
enabled at $h\cdot x$, with the same footprints, and its proposal there is $h$
applied to its proposal at $x$. Second, the law's invariants hold at $x$
exactly when they hold at $h\cdot x$. A realizer of the law is
\term[gauge-covariant realizer]{gauge covariant} when it selects at $h\cdot x$
the same moves as at $x$: a deterministic realizer the same batch, a
relational one the same set of batches, a stochastic one the same weights, and
a coherent one, the quantum kind of \cref{ch:quantum-gauge} that attaches
coefficients to moves, the same coefficients.

title: Gauge covariance passes to runs
label: prop:gauge-runs
section: A law on a gauge frame
statement:
For a gauge-covariant law with a gauge-covariant deterministic realizer,
$F(h\cdot x)=h\cdot F(x)$ for every gauge change $h$ and every legal state
$x$. The runs from $x$ and from $h\cdot x$ are related tick by tick by $h$,
and every gauge-invariant reading takes the same values along both.

title: Five ticks read the outside
label: prop:five-ticks
section: A law on a gauge frame
statement:
Under the pose law, five ticks carry the pose at $v_0$ once round the outside
of $K$:
\[
g^{(5)}_{v_0}=U_{e_4}U_{e_3}U_{e_7}U_{e_6}U_{e_5}U_{e_1}\,g_{v_0},
\]
the holonomy \eqref{eq:path-holonomy} of the outside, based at $v_0$, applied
to the pose. Likewise at $v_2$, $v_3$, $v_4$ and $v_5$, with the loop based
there. The pose at $v_1$ is carried over $e_2$ and straight back at every
tick, and is never turned.

title: Discrete Stokes and divergence theorems
label: prop:discrete-stokes
statement:
Let the canvas carry its stored orientation, each face read anticlockwise.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\curl D=0$ and $\divg\curl^*=0$: a difference has no curl, and an
  adjoint curl has no divergence.
\item \emph{Stokes.} For a set $S$ of faces, $\sum_{f\in S}\curl A(f)$ is the
  sum of $A$ round the boundary of $S$: over the edges that lie on exactly one
  face of $S$, each read as that face reads it.
\item \emph{Divergence.} For a set $U$ of vertices, $\sum_{v\in U}\divg E(v)$
  is the sum of $E$ over the edges with exactly one end in $U$, each read in
  the direction leaving $U$.
\item \emph{Summation by parts.} Summing over the stored edges,
  \begin{gather*}
  \textstyle\sum_e D\phi(e)\,E(e)=-\sum_v\phi(v)\divg E(v),\\
  \textstyle\sum_f\curl A(f)\,B(f)=\sum_e A(e)\curl^*B(e).
  \end{gather*}
\end{enumerate}

title: Reversing a tick of two steps
label: prop:two-step-reversal
statement:
Let a tick be $F=S_1\circ S_0$, and let an involution $R$ of the states undo
each step: $R\circ S_0\circ R=S_0^{-1}$ and $R\circ S_1\circ R=S_1^{-1}$. Then
$I_0=R\circ S_0$ and $I_1=S_1\circ R$ are involutions, and each reverses the
tick:
\[
I_0\circ F\circ I_0=F^{-1}=I_1\circ F\circ I_1 .
\]

title: Closed-window conservation
label: thm:closed-window
statement:
If the local continuity equation holds on a finite canvas, its total charge
is constant in time. So is the total charge of a window of a larger canvas, if
no edge that leaves the window carries flux.

title: No-signalling halo
label: def:no-signalling
section: Laws as patterns on the temporal \texorpdfstring{\mbox{prism}~\optionalmark}{prism}
statement:
Let $H$ assign to each cell $y$ a set $H(y)$ of cells, and write $H(V)$ for
the cells in the halos of the cells of a set $V$. It is a
\term[no-signalling halo]{no-signalling halo} of a realizer when, for every set $V$ of cells, what the next tick may show on $V$ depends
only on the table on $H(V)$: the tables on $V$ that some allowed step shows,
for a deterministic or a relational realizer, and their weights, for a
stochastic one.

title: What a strung run fixes
label: prop:run-fixes
section: Laws as patterns on the temporal \texorpdfstring{\mbox{prism}~\optionalmark}{prism}
statement:
Among deterministic laws that read a declared halo and act alike at every
cell, a run fixes the law exactly on the windows it shows: the tables on a
halo that occur in the run, each with the value it leads to. If $u$ windows
never occur, $|A|^u$ laws agree with the run, for $A$ the values of a cell.

title: Count; weave; strand
label: def:weave
section: Laws as patterns on the temporal \texorpdfstring{\mbox{prism}~\optionalmark}{prism}
statement:
A \term{count} gives each value $a$ of a cell $y$ a number $c_y(a)$ of
\term[token]{tokens}, with no tokens on the value $0$; the count of a table
$x$ is $N(x)=\sum_yc_y(x(y))$. A law \term[keeping a count]{keeps} the count
when every step its realizer allows keeps $N$. A \term{weave} of a step
$x\to x'$ along a halo $H$ pairs the tokens of $x$ one to one with the tokens
of $x'$, each token moving from a cell $u$ to a cell $y$ only when $u$ lies in
$H(y)$. The weaves of the ticks of a run, joined end to end, string its tokens
as \term[strand!of a token]{strands}: paths that neither begin nor end and
step only along the stencils.

title: Hall; supplies and demands
label: thm:hall
section: Laws as patterns on the temporal \texorpdfstring{\mbox{prism}~\optionalmark}{prism}
statement:
Let finitely many stores hold goods $s(u)\ge0$ and finitely many shops need
goods $d(y)\ge0$, with equal totals, and let each store be allowed to supply
some of the shops. All the goods can be sent along allowed pairs, every need
met, if and only if every set $U$ of stores holds at most what the shops it
may supply need together.

title: A kept count is woven
label: thm:woven
section: Laws as patterns on the temporal \texorpdfstring{\mbox{prism}~\optionalmark}{prism}
statement:
Let every table obtained from a legal table by emptying cells, setting their
values to $0$, be legal. Let $H$ be a no-signalling halo of a realizer, and
let the law keep a count. Then every step $x\to x'$ the realizer allows has a
weave along $H$. Conversely, a step that has a weave keeps the count.

title: Symmetries of a slot tapestry
label: prop:slot-symmetry
section: Laws as patterns on the temporal \texorpdfstring{\mbox{prism}~\optionalmark}{prism}
statement:
Applying $h$ at every slot and shifting by $j$ carries every run of the
slots to a run if and only if $h\circ S_{(s+j)\bmod k}\circ h^{-1}=S_s$ for every $s$; then
$h\circ P_j$ commutes with the tick. Applying $h$, reversing time and
shifting by $j$ does so if and only if
$h\circ S_{(j-1-s)\bmod k}^{-1}\circ h^{-1}=S_s$ for every $s$; then
$h\circ P_j$ reverses the tick: $(h\circ P_j)\circ F\circ(h\circ P_j)^{-1}=F^{-1}$.

title: Symmetry of what may happen
label: thm:curie
section: Laws as patterns on the temporal \texorpdfstring{\mbox{prism}~\optionalmark}{prism}
statement:
Let every motion of a group $G$ be a symmetry of a law, and let the motions
of a subgroup $S$ fix the start $x_0$. Then every motion of $S$ carries the
runs from $x_0$ to runs from $x_0$, so the set of states reachable at each
tick is carried to itself by $S$. If a stochastic realizer commutes with $G$,
the weight of each state at each tick is the weight of its image under $S$.

title: Breaking needs a choice
label: prop:breaking
section: Laws as patterns on the temporal \texorpdfstring{\mbox{prism}~\optionalmark}{prism}

title: Reversibility
label: thm:reversible
statement:
For fixed source current $J$, the Maxwell macro-tick is bijective on the finite
state space.

title: Time reversal of the Maxwell tick
label: cor:maxwell-reversal
statement:
The map
\[
I(A,E,J,\rho)=(-A-E,\;E,\;-J,\;\rho)
\]
is an involution that reads each link and each site alone, and
$I\circ F\circ I=F^{-1}$. A run read backwards through $I$ is a run.

title: Gauge covariance of the Maxwell tick
label: thm:maxwell-covariant
statement:
For fixed source $J$, the Maxwell macro-tick commutes with the gauge action
$A\mapsto A+Dg$ of \eqref{eq:gauge-formula}, the additive form of
\eqref{eq:gauge-action}, which fixes $E$, $\rho$ and $J$: if $(A,E)$ goes to
$(A',E')$, then $(A+Dg,E)$ goes to $(A'+Dg,E')$. The law of this section is
gauge covariant in the sense of \cref{def:gauge-covariant-law}, and so is its
realizer, which takes every link at every phase.

title: Gauss preservation
label: thm:gauss-preserved
section: Gauss law rides with the dynamics
statement:
If the pre-tick state satisfies Gauss and the source transition satisfies
continuity, then the post-kick state satisfies $\divg E'=\rho'$.

title: The Maxwell shears keep the canonical pairing
label: lem:maxwell-pairing
section: Gauss law rides with the dynamics
statement:
On states $(A,E)$ put
$\Omega\bigl((A,E),(a,e)\bigr)=\langle A,e\rangle-\langle E,a\rangle$, where
$\langle\,,\rangle$ multiplies link tables link by link, each link once in its
stored orientation, and adds. $\Omega$ is
perfect, and the source-free kick $E\mapsto E+\curl^*\curl A$ and the move
$A\mapsto A-E$ each keep it.

title: Gauss's law from the tally of gauge symmetry
label: cor:gauss-noether
section: Gauss law rides with the dynamics
statement:
For every site function $g$, the source-free tick fixes the table
$w_g=(Dg,0)$, and the conserved tally that \cref{thm:noether} pairs with it
is
\[
\Omega\bigl(w_g,(A,E)\bigr)=\langle Dg,E\rangle=-\langle g,\divg E\rangle .
\]
With no source, $\divg E$ is therefore kept at every site. With a source $J$
the tick is affine with source $b=(J,-J)$, the tally changes at every tick by
$\Omega(w_g,b)=\langle g,\divg J\rangle$, and continuity
$\rho'-\rho+\divg J=0$ turns this into the conservation of $\divg E-\rho$:
\cref{thm:gauss-preserved}, read as Noether's identity.

title: A gauge change that varies from tick to tick
label: prop:gauge-defect
section: Gauss law rides with the dynamics
statement:
Let $(A_t,E_t,\rho_t)$ be a run of the Maxwell tick, and replace each $A_t$ by
$A_t+D\chi_t$. The new frame keeps every kick and Gauss's law at every tick,
and each Faraday move fails by exactly $D(\chi_{t+1}-\chi_t)$:
\[
A_{t+1}+D\chi_{t+1}=(A_t+D\chi_t)-E_{t+1}+D(\chi_{t+1}-\chi_t).
\]

title: Temporal links
label: def:temporal-links
section: Gauss law rides with the dynamics
statement:
A \term[temporal link]{temporal-link} table $a_0(t)$ is a site function for
each tick, its value at $v$ standing on the temporal link from $(v,t)$ to
$(v,t+1)$. The \term[extended Maxwell tick]{extended} tick keeps the kick and
moves the potential by $A'=A-E'+Da_0(t)$. A gauge change by site functions
$\chi_t$ adds $D\chi_t$ to the potential at tick $t$ and $\chi_{t+1}-\chi_t$ to
the temporal links from tick $t$.

title: Temporal links
label: thm:temporal-links
section: Gauss law rides with the dynamics
statement:
Let the tick be the extended tick of \cref{def:temporal-links}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every gauge change carries runs of the extended tick to runs.
\item The gauge change with $\chi_0=0$ and $\chi_{t+1}=\chi_t-a_0(t)$ carries
  every run of the extended tick to one whose temporal links are all $0$,
  that is, to a run of the Maxwell tick of \cref{sec:maxwell-tick}, with the
  same electric field, the same $\curl A$ and the same $\divg E-\rho$ at every
  tick.
\end{enumerate}

title: Gauge covariance of a hop
label: prop:hop-covariance
section: The two-component walk, and its coupling
statement:
The coupled hop commutes with the simultaneous gauge action on $A$ and
$\psi$.

title: What the two steps force
label: prop:maxwell-shape
section: What is forced, and what is chosen?
statement:
Let a law on the links of a square window carry $A$ and $E$, with no
current, and let
its score open two steps in turn: a kick that adds to the $E$ of every link a
value $\varphi(A)$ computed from $A$ on the faces at that link, and a move that adds
to the $A$ of every link a value computed from that link's new $E$. Suppose
that both additions are additive and the same at every face and every link,
that the kick is blind to gauge changes, $\varphi(A+Dg)=\varphi(A)$ for every
site function $g$, and that it keeps Gauss's law, $\divg\varphi(A)=0$ for every
$A$.
Then for some $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ in $\Zmod8$
\[
E'=E+\kappa\curl^*\curl A,\qquad A'=A-\lambda E'.
\]
Conversely, every such pair of steps is reversible and gauge covariant, and
it keeps Gauss's law.

title: Native coefficient ring
label: qr:ring
statement:
The coefficients of this chapter lie in
\[
 R_8=\Z[1/\sqrt2,\zeta]=\Z[1/2,\sqrt2,i].
\]
Its numerical reading takes $\sqrt2$ to the positive square root of two
and $i$ to the chosen quarter-turn. Every coefficient has unique
coordinates
\[
 a+b\sqrt2+i(c+d\sqrt2),\qquad a,b,c,d\in\Z[1/2].
\]
Here $\Z[1/2]$ consists of integers divided by powers of two.

title: Coherent composition
label: qr:coherent-composition
section: From applications to a coherent law
statement:
For two consecutive finite phases $U$ and $V$, the coefficient from $x$ to $z$ is
\[
 (VU)[z,x]=\sum_y V[z,y]U[y,x].
\]
For a finite history $h=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, its coefficient is
\[
 \prod_{t=1}^n U_t[x_t,x_{t-1}].
\]
The coefficient at a complete final
endpoint $z$ is the sum of these products over histories ending at $z$.

title: A kept count is woven: coherent laws
label: cor:qr-woven
section: From applications to a coherent law
statement:
Let a script keep a count: every step $x\to x'$ with $U[x',x]\ne0$ keeps it.
Then each such step has a weave along every no-signalling halo of the script.

title: The selected native probability law
label: qr:selected-law
statement:
Under V, Z, AE, $D_2$, $N_1$, O and the stated finite resource schema,
the unique probability law on admitted complete columns is
\[
 \pi_\psi(z)=|\psi_z|^2.
\]
For different independent preparations the joint law is consequently
the product of their laws.

title: The colourless three-quark state
label: prop:mp-epsilon
chapter: What a model of matter must explain
section: Colour, and why the group is \texorpdfstring{$SU(3)$}{SU(3)}
statement:
Let $g\in GL(3,\C)$ act on $V\otimes V\otimes V$ by
$g\otimes g\otimes g$. Then
$(g\otimes g\otimes g)\,\varepsilon=\det(g)\,\varepsilon$. Hence
$\varepsilon$ is fixed by $g$ if and only if $\det g=1$, and
contraction with $\varepsilon$ is an intertwiner in the sense of
\cref{def:intertwiner} for a group $G\le GL(3,\C)$ exactly when
$G\le SL(3,\C)$.

title: Triality
label: prop:mp-triality
chapter: What a model of matter must explain
statement:
The centre of $SU(3)$ is $\{I,\omega I,\omega^2I\}$ with
$\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}$. On a state of $q$ quarks and $\bar q$
antiquarks the element $\omega I$ acts as multiplication by
$\omega^{\,q-\bar q}$. A colourless state therefore has
$q-\bar q\equiv0\pmod3$.

title: Left and right writes
label: def:mt-writes
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: A link that does not commute
statement:
For $h\in G$ the \term{left write} and the \term{right write} act on a
table by
\[
(L_h\psi)(U)=\psi(h^{-1}U),\qquad (R_h\psi)(U)=\psi(Uh).
\]
Each is a legal application with coefficient one: it moves the
coefficient at $U$ to the cell $hU$, or to $Uh^{-1}$, without changing coefficient values.

title: The two write families
label: prop:mt-writes
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: A link that does not commute
statement:
Left and right writes commute with each other, $L_hR_k=R_kL_h$ for all
$h,k$. A gauge change $(h_x,h_y)$ acts on the link's coefficient table by
one write of each kind,
\[
\psi\longmapsto L_{h_y}R_{h_x}\psi,\qquad
(L_{h_y}R_{h_x}\psi)(U)=\psi(h_y^{-1}Uh_x),
\]
the table that assigns to the moved link $h_yUh_x^{-1}$ the coefficient
the old table assigned to $U$.

title: Block of an irreducible representation
label: def:mt-block
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: Electric blocks, and the one-edge operators
statement:
Let $\rho:G\to GL(d_\rho,\C)$ be an irreducible representation. Its
\term{block} in the table space is
\[
B_\rho=\{\,U\mapsto\Tr(A\rho(U))\;:\;A\in\mathrm{Mat}_{d_\rho}(\C)\,\},
\]
a space of tables of dimension $d_\rho^2$, on which a left write acts by
$A\mapsto A\rho(h)^{-1}$ and a right write by $A\mapsto\rho(h)A$.

title: Blocks fill the table space
label: thm:mt-blocks
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: Electric blocks, and the one-edge operators
statement:
The blocks of the distinct irreducible representations are independent,
orthogonal for the pairing of \cref{qr:hilbert}, and together span the
complex-valued tables: $\sum_\rho d_\rho^2=|G|$. Every left and right
write carries each block into itself.

title: Averaging counts
label: prop:mt-average
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: Electric blocks, and the one-edge operators
statement:
For a representation $W$ of $G$, the average $\frac1{|G|}\sum_UW(U)$ is
the projector onto the vectors fixed by $G$, so the number of independent
fixed vectors is $\frac1{|G|}\sum_U\chi_W(U)$. For two irreducible
characters, $\frac1{|G|}\sum_U\chi_\rho(U)\overline{\chi_\sigma(U)}$ is
$1$ when $\rho=\sigma$ and $0$ otherwise; hence the number of times
$\rho$ occurs in $W$ is $\frac1{|G|}\sum_U\chi_W(U)\overline{\chi_\rho(U)}$.

title: One-edge operators
label: thm:mt-convolution
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: Electric blocks, and the one-edge operators
statement:
A matrix on the table space commutes with all left and right writes if
and only if it is convolution by a class function $f$,
\[
(f*\psi)(V)=\sum_{U\in G}f(VU^{-1})\,\psi(U)=\sum_{h\in G}f(h)\,(L_h\psi)(V).
\]
Convolution by $f$ acts on the block $B_\rho$ as the scalar
$\hat f(\rho)=\frac1{d_\rho}\sum_Uf(U)\overline{\chi_\rho(U)}$. Writing
$f=\frac1{|G|}\sum_\rho r(\rho)\,d_\rho\,\chi_\rho$, the scalar on
$B_\rho$ is $r(\rho)$, so the operator is unitary exactly when every $r(\rho)$
is a unit phase.

title: Electric response and electric read
label: def:mt-response
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: Electric blocks, and the one-edge operators
statement:
An \term{electric response} is a unit phase $r(\rho)$ for every
irreducible representation, with $r(\mathbf1)=1$. Its \term{electric
read} is convolution by the kernel
\[
k=\frac1{|G|}\sum_{\rho}r(\rho)\,d_\rho\,\chi_\rho,\qquad
\mathcal K\psi=k*\psi=\sum_{h\in G}k(h)\,L_h\psi ,
\]
the unique operator that multiplies each block by its response and
commutes with the gauge action.

title: Six native sign reads on the cube group
label: prop:mt-native-reads
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: Electric blocks, and the one-edge operators
statement:
Allowing either sign on the trivial block, of the thirty nonconstant
sign assignments on $S_4$, exactly six
have kernels in $R_8$: $D=\{\mathbf3_{\mathrm r}\}$,
$\{\mathbf3_{\mathrm s}\}$, $\{\mathbf3_{\mathrm r},\mathbf3_{\mathrm s}\}$
and their complements. Complementing $D$ negates the whole kernel.
Thus exactly three nonidentity responses obey the normalization
$r(\mathbf1)=1$ of \cref{def:mt-response}: the three displayed sets.
For $D=\{\mathbf3_{\mathrm r},\mathbf3_{\mathrm s}\}$
the kernel is $-\tfrac12$ at the identity, $+\tfrac12$ at each of the
three half-turns about face axes, and zero elsewhere. For a single
triplet it is $\pm\tfrac14$ on the sixteen elements that are not
third-turns.

title: Declared electric energy
label: def:mt-energy
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: From a phase to an energy
statement:
An \term{electric energy table} is a function $E:\Irr(G)\to\Q$ with
$E(\mathbf1)=0$ and $E(\rho)>0$ otherwise. The \term{electric energy}
of a link is the operator $H_E$ that multiplies the block $B_\rho$ by
$E(\rho)$: convolution by $\frac1{|G|}\sum_\rho E(\rho)d_\rho\chi_\rho$,
which commutes with the gauge action by \cref{thm:mt-convolution}.

title: Sign rule
label: def:mt-sign-rule
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
statement:
For an occupation table $n$ and a mode $m$, let $p(n,m)$ be the number of
occupied modes that precede $m$ in the chosen order. Then
\begin{align*}
a^\dagger_m|n\rangle&=(-1)^{p(n,m)}|n+1_m\rangle\quad\text{if }n_m=0,\\
a_m|n\rangle&=(-1)^{p(n,m)}|n-1_m\rangle\quad\text{if }n_m=1,
\end{align*}
and both give the zero table otherwise.

title: The order is a presentation
label: prop:mt-order-witness
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
statement:
Changing the order of the modes conjugates every creation and every
annihilation by one diagonal matrix $\Sigma$ of signs, the same for all
of them. Every operator built from them is conjugated by $\Sigma$, every
occupation number $n_m=a^\dagger_ma_m$ is unchanged, and every report,
which reads squared sizes of coefficients on basis states, is unchanged.

title: Second quantization is a homomorphism
label: prop:mt-gamma
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
statement:
$\Gamma(g_2)\Gamma(g_1)=\Gamma(g_2g_1)$, and
$\Gamma(g)\,a^\dagger_{cs}\,\Gamma(g)^{-1}=\sum_{c'}g_{c'c}a^\dagger_{c's}$.
For a unitary $g$, $\Gamma(g)$ is unitary.

title: Colourless states of one edge
label: def:mt-colourless
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: Colourless states, and how to count them
statement:
A state is \term{colourless} when every gauge pair fixes it,
\[
\psi(h_yUh_x^{-1})=\Gamma_x(h_x)\Gamma_y(h_y)\,\psi(U)\qquad
\text{for all }h_x,h_y,U .
\]
It lies in the \term{zero-flux sector} when, in addition, $\psi$ is
constant in $U$: the link's table lies in the trivial block, and each end
is then colourless on its own. This space is the tensor product of
the two local invariant spaces, including linear combinations of
product states.

title: Colourless states are the invariants of one vertex
label: prop:mt-gauge-fix
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: Colourless states, and how to count them
statement:
A colourless state is determined by its value at the identity link,
$\psi(1)$, and $\psi(1)$ can be any vector fixed by the diagonal action
$\Gamma_x(h)\Gamma_y(h)$. Hence the colourless states of one edge with
$d$ slots correspond to the invariant occupation tables of one vertex
with $2d$ slots. The zero-flux space is the tensor product of the
invariant spaces at $x$ and $y$.

title: Census of colourless states
label: thm:mt-census
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
