section: Colourless states, and how to count them
statement:
On one edge with $d$ slots, the number of colourless states with $k$
quarks is the coefficient of $z^k$ in
\[
\frac1{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\bigl(1+\chi(g)z+\overline{\chi(g)}z^2+z^3\bigr)^{2d},
\]
a sum over conjugacy classes weighted by their sizes. The zero-flux
states with $k_x$ quarks at $x$ and $k_y$ at $y$ number the product of
the coefficients of $z^{k_x}$ and $z^{k_y}$ in the same average with
exponent $d$.

title: The hop is covariant
label: prop:mt-hop-covariant
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: The hop, its coin, and a native tick
statement:
For all gauge pairs and link values,
\[
\Gamma_x(h_x)\Gamma_y(h_y)\,V_U\,\Gamma_y(h_y)^{-1}\Gamma_x(h_x)^{-1}
=V_{h_yUh_x^{-1}} .
\]
Hence $V$ commutes with the gauge action of
$G\times G$ on link and matter together, and maps colourless states to
colourless states.

title: The coin's coefficients are minors
label: prop:mt-minors
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: The hop, its coin, and a native tick
statement:
The coefficient of $\Gamma(W)$ from the $k$-quark state with occupied
modes $m_1<\cdots<m_k$ to the one with occupied modes
$m'_1<\cdots<m'_k$ is the $k\times k$ minor of $W$ with rows
$m'_1,\ldots,m'_k$ and columns $m_1,\ldots,m_k$. Hence the coefficients
of $\Gamma(W_U)$ lie in $R_8$ for every link value of the cube group, and
$\Gamma(W_U)$ is unitary.

title: The tick preserves the colourless sector
label: thm:mt-tick-gauss
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: The hop, its coin, and a native tick
statement:
$T$ commutes with the gauge action of $G\times G$. Hence it maps
colourless states to colourless states, and is unitary on them.

title: Link moments
label: prop:mt-moments
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: The hop, its coin, and a native tick
statement:
For an irreducible triplet of a finite subgroup of $SU(3)$, using a
real orthonormal basis when the triplet is real,
\begin{align*}
\frac1{|G|}\sum_UU&=0,\qquad
\frac1{|G|}\sum_UU_{ij}\overline{U_{kl}}=\frac{\delta_{ik}\delta_{jl}}3,\\
\frac1{|G|}\sum_UU_{ij}U_{kl}&=
\begin{cases}\delta_{ik}\delta_{jl}/3&\text{if the triplet is real,}\\[2pt]
0&\text{if }\mathbf3\otimes\mathbf3\text{ has no invariant,}\end{cases}
\end{align*}
and when $\mathbf3^{\otimes3}$ has exactly one invariant,
$\frac1{|G|}\sum_UU_{ij}U_{kl}U_{mn}=\varepsilon_{ikm}\varepsilon_{jln}/6$.

title: The there-and-back tally
label: thm:mt-there-and-back
chapter: Links that do not commute, and matter that excludes
section: The hop, its coin, and a native tick
statement:
Let $P$ be the projector onto the zero-flux sector, and
$A_{cc'}=\sum_sa^\dagger_{ycs}a_{xc's}$. Then $PVP=0$, the hop moves
the link's table into the triplet block or its conjugate, and
\begin{align*}
PV^2P&=\Omega,\\
\Omega&=\frac13\sum_{c,c'}\bigl(A^\dagger_{cc'}A_{cc'}+A_{cc'}A^\dagger_{cc'}\bigr)\\
&\quad+\frac{m}3\sum_{c,c'}\bigl(A_{cc'}A_{cc'}+A^\dagger_{cc'}A^\dagger_{cc'}\bigr),
\end{align*}
with $m=1$ for a real triplet and $m=0$ when $\mathbf3\otimes\mathbf3$
has no invariant, both sides restricted to the sector. Consequently the
family of coins $\Gamma(e^{i\theta K_U})=e^{i\theta V_U}$, of which the
native coin is the member $\theta=\pi/4$, returns to the sector as
\[
P\,\mathcal C_\theta\,P=P-\frac{\theta^2}2\,\Omega+O(\theta^3),
\]
and the second-order shift of the energy law \eqref{eq:mt-energy-law}
on the sector is $-\Omega/(\kappa E_3)$.

title: The eight invariants of a vertex with two slots
label: prop:mm-two-slot-invariants
section: Model I: the rotations of the cube
statement:
For the cube group with two slots, the colourless states of one vertex
number $1,0,1,4,1,0,1$ by quark number, eight in all, and the eight
states of \cref{fig:mm-two-slot-invariants} are a basis of them. Six
of the eight are fixed by $SU(3)$; the pair and the paired holes are
not.

title: Every extra state is located in one average
label: thm:mm-census-moments
section: Model I: the rotations of the cube
statement:
Let $G\le SU(3)$ be a finite colour group with triplet character
$\chi$. The number of colourless states with $n$ quarks on one edge
with $d$ slots is
\[
\sum_{a+2b+3c=n}\frac{(2d)!}{a!\,b!\,c!\,(2d-a-b-c)!}\,
\langle\chi^a\bar\chi^{\,b}\rangle ,
\]
the sum over $a,b,c\ge0$ with $a+b+c\le2d$. Every average of $G$ is at
least the corresponding count for $SU(3)$, so every entry of the
census of $G$ is at least the entry for $SU(3)$, and the difference is
the same sum taken over the differences of the averages.

title: The pair is bound more tightly than the quartet
label: prop:mm-diquark
statement:
On the two-quark zero-flux sector of Model I, spanned by the pair at
$x$ and the pair at $y$ with unit norm,
\[
\Omega=\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&2\end{pmatrix},
\]
with the value $4$ on the sum of the two pairs and $0$ on their
difference. Without the pair-hop term $\Omega$ is $2$ on both. The
quartet at one vertex has $\Omega=3$.

title: The spectrum of the tally on one edge
label: thm:mm-spectra
statement:
On the $36$ zero-flux states of the $SU(3)$-type models the tally has
the values $0^9\,3^{16}\,4^5\,6^2\,(20/3)^3\,8^1$, multiplicities as
exponents. On the $64$ states of Model I it has
$0^{14}\,3^{32}\,4^{10}\,(20/3)^6\,8^2$. The largest value, $8$, is
reached once in the first case and twice in the second: once by a
state with three quarks at each end, and once by a state on the chain
of \cref{fig:mm-chain}. With the pair-hop term removed by hand the
spectrum on the $64$ states is
$0^9\,2^4\,(8/3)^2\,3^{32}\,(10/3)^2\,4^9\,6^2\,(20/3)^3\,8^1$, and $8$
is reached once.

title: The two-baryon states are ordered by spin
label: prop:mm-spin-order
statement:
The sixteen states with three quarks at each end are the products of
the two quartets, and $\Omega$ commutes with $S_z$ on them. By $S_z$
the sector splits into $1,2,3,4,3,2,1$ states for $S_z=3,\ldots,-3$,
and on the sectors $|S_z|=3,2,1,0$ the tally has the values $\{0\}$,
$\{0,4\}$, $\{0,4,\tfrac{20}3\}$ and $\{0,4,\tfrac{20}3,8\}$. Read
with the spin ladder, the seven states of spin $3$ carry $0$, the five
of spin $2$ carry $4$, the three of spin $1$ carry $\tfrac{20}3$, and
the one state of spin $0$ carries $8$. The sector and its tally are
the same in all five models.

title: The pair hop is the cause
label: prop:mm-control
statement:
Remove the pair-hop term from $\Omega$ by hand, leaving the two
there-and-back histories with the moment $\tfrac13$. Then on the
sixty-four states the value $8$ is reached once, by the spin-zero
two-baryon state; the pair drops to $2$, below the quartet's $3$; and
the chain of \cref{fig:mm-chain} falls apart into the two full vertices
at $6$ and the two mixed states at $\tfrac{10}3$. The values $2$,
$\tfrac83$ and $\tfrac{10}3$, which no $SU(3)$-type state takes,
appear only in this control.

title: A symmetry that only a real triplet has
label: prop:mm-particle-hole
statement:
On the sixty-four zero-flux states of Model I, $\mathcal S$ and the parity
$(-1)^{N_x}$ commute with $\Omega$ and anticommute with each other. Every value
of $\Omega$ there has even multiplicity, and $\mathcal S$ exchanges the two
states at the ground value $8$: the spin-zero two-baryon state, of odd parity,
and the chain of pairs, of even parity. Without the pair hop, $\mathcal S$ does
not commute with $\Omega$.

title: The sixty rotations
label: prop:mm-icosahedron
statement:
Every vertex $v$ of the icosahedron has $v\cdot v=\varphi+2$, and with
respect to $v$ the twelve vertices are $v$ itself, five neighbours with
$v\cdot w=\varphi$, five vertices with $v\cdot w=-\varphi$, and the
antipode $-v$. A rotation of the icosahedron is determined by the
images of one vertex and one of its neighbours, so there are at most
$12\cdot5=60$. For each pair of neighbours $(w_1,w_2)$ the matrix that
carries the frame $(v_1,v_2,v_1\times v_2)$ to $(w_1,w_2,w_1\times w_2)$
is a rotation with entries in $\tfrac12\Z[\varphi]$, and all sixty
carry the vertex set to itself. Their traces are $3$ once, $-1$
fifteen times, $0$ twenty times, $\varphi$ twelve times and
$1-\varphi$ twelve times.

title: The tensor square of the icosahedral triplet
label: prop:mm-a5-tensor
statement:
For the icosahedral group,
$\mathbf3\otimes\mathbf3=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf3\oplus\mathbf5$, with
$\Lambda^2\mathbf3=\mathbf3$ and $\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathbf3=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf5$,
and $\langle\chi^4\rangle=3$. For the cube group,
$\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathbf3_{\mathrm r}=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf2\oplus\mathbf3_{\mathrm s}$
and $\langle\chi^4\rangle=4$.

title: Models I and II share their zero-flux sector
label: prop:mm-same-sector
statement:
The eight states of \cref{fig:mm-two-slot-invariants} are the
one-vertex invariants of Model II as well, the zero-flux sectors of
the two models are the same sixty-four states, and their tallies
$\Omega$ are the same operator, with the spectrum of
\cref{thm:mm-spectra}.

title: The group $C_3\times A_5$ and its triplet
label: def:mm-centre
statement:
The colour group of Refinement I is $C_3\times A_5$: the pairs
$(\omega^j,g)$ with $j\in\{0,1,2\}$ and $g$ an icosahedral rotation,
multiplied componentwise. Its triplet is $(\omega^j,g)\mapsto\omega^jg$,
a unitary matrix of determinant $\omega^{3j}\det g=1$. The group has
$180$ elements and contains the centre of $SU(3)$; its character is
$\chi(\omega^j,g)=\omega^j\chi_{\mathbf3}(g)$, with values in
$\Z[\omega,\varphi]$.

title: Triality, and the pair moment
label: prop:mm-centre
statement:
For Refinement I the census vanishes at every quark number that is not
a multiple of three; the pair moment is $\langle\chi^2\rangle=0$, so
the pair hop is absent and $m=0$ in \cref{thm:mt-there-and-back}; the
one-vertex invariants at two slots are the six states of
\cref{fig:mm-two-slot-invariants} that $SU(3)$ fixes; and the
zero-flux sector and the tally are those of the first row of
\cref{fig:mm-exchange-spectra}, with the ground value $8$ reached once.

title: Orders from traces
label: prop:mm-s1080-orders
statement:
A unitary $3\times3$ matrix of determinant one with a real trace $t$ has the
eigenvalues $1$, $e^{i\theta}$ and $e^{-i\theta}$ with
$1+2\cos\theta=t$; with the trace $\omega^jt$, $t$ real, its
eigenvalues are $\omega^j$ times these. Every trace in
\cref{fig:mm-s1080-classes} has this form, and the orders in the table
follow: $1$, $2$, $3$ (four classes), $4$, $5$ (two), $6$ (two), $12$
(two) and $15$ (four). The exponent of the group, the least $e$ with
$g^e=1$ for every $g$, is $60$.

title: The tensor squares of the Valentiner triplet
label: prop:mm-s1080-tensor
statement:
For $S(1080)$, $\langle\chi\bar\chi\rangle=1$ and
$\langle\chi^2\bar\chi^2\rangle=2$. Hence
$\mathbf3\otimes\bar{\mathbf3}=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf8$ with the eight
irreducible, and $\mathbf3\otimes\mathbf3=\bar{\mathbf3}\oplus\mathbf6$
with the six irreducible: the shapes of $SU(3)$. For $C_3\times A_5$
the second average is $3$, and the eight splits as
$\mathbf3\oplus\mathbf5$.

title: Agreement with $SU(3)$ at two slots
label: thm:mm-s1080-agreement
statement:
On one edge with two slots, Refinement II has the census of $SU(3)$,
$92$ states with the same distribution by quark number, the same
zero-flux sector of $36$ states, and the same tally. The first
edge-census difference is already at three slots per vertex: at six
quarks the counts are $491$ and $490$, and at twelve quarks the same
counts recur. Every other count at three slots agrees. At four slots
per vertex, at six quarks $S(1080)$ has
$28$ colourless states more than $SU(3)$, all charged to
$\langle\chi^6\rangle=6$ against $5$, one invariant of degree six in
the triplet that $SU(3)$ does not have. The full four-slot census is
$59\,560$ against $58\,202$, with the extras $28$, $280$, $742$,
$280$ and $28$ at $6$, $9$, $12$, $15$ and $18$ quarks.

title: Every loop closes
label: thm:mm-loop
section: What none of the models catch
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite colour group with exponent $e$. For every
connection $U$ on every canvas and every loop $\gamma$,
$\Hol_U(\gamma)^e=1$: a quark transported $e$ times around any loop
returns with its colour unchanged, and the Wilson loop of the
$e$-fold loop is $3$. For the four models $e=12$, $30$, $30$ and $60$.
No $e$ does this for $SU(3)$.

title: Colourless states of a path
label: prop:ml-path
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
On a path whose matter sits at the two ends, a colourless state depends
on the links only through their product, the holonomy
$P=U_R\cdots U_1$ of \eqref{eq:path-holonomy}, and the colourless
states of the path are the colourless states of one edge with link
$P$. With a quark source at $x_0$, an antiquark source at $x_R$ and $d$
slots at each end, their number with $k$ dynamical quarks is the
coefficient of $z^k$ in
\[
\bigl\langle\chi(g)\,\overline{\chi(g)}\,\det(1+zg)^{2d}\bigr\rangle_G .
\]

title: The string
label: thm:ml-string
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
Let a quark source sit at $x_0$ and an antiquark source at $x_R$, with
no dynamical quarks.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each of the five colour groups there is one colourless line, spanned by
the \term{string}
\[
\psi_{cc'}(U_1,\ldots,U_R)=\bigl(U_1^{-1}U_2^{-1}\cdots U_R^{-1}\bigr)_{cc'}
=\overline{(U_R\cdots U_1)_{c'c}},
\]
with $c$ the source index at $x_0$ and $c'$ the one at $x_R$: the
antiquark's colour transported back along the path to the quark. On
every link its table lies in the conjugate triplet block, declared at
the level $E_3$ and equal to the triplet block when the triplet is
real, so under the declared law its electric energy is $\kappa E_3R$:
one level per link, linear in the length. No hop acts on it, and it is
an eigenstate of $H$.
\item With two quark sources in place of a quark and an antiquark
there is a colourless state exactly when the triplet is real,
$\langle\chi^2\rangle=1$, and it is the same string. For a complex
triplet there is none: no string of any length joins two quarks.
\end{enumerate}

title: The screening number
label: prop:ml-screening
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
The least number of dynamical quarks with which both sources are
colourless without flux is $2$ when the triplet is real and $3$ when
it is complex. In the first case one quark sits at each source, in
either spin: four states. In the second, two quarks in the
antisymmetric colour pair sit at the quark source, in any of the three
symmetric spin states, and one at the antiquark source: six states.

title: Where the string and screened levels cross
label: prop:ml-breaking
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
For a quark source and an antiquark source at distance $R$, the
unscreened string has lower electric-plus-mass energy than the
minimal zero-flux screened state while
\[
\kappa E_3R<k_{\min}M,\qquad
k_{\min}=\begin{cases}2&\text{real triplet,}\\3&\text{complex triplet,}\end{cases}
\]
and a screened state of \cref{prop:ml-screening} is lower beyond. With
$E_3=\tfrac43$ the crossing is at $R=3M/(2\kappa)$ for the rotation
groups and at $R=9M/(4\kappa)$ for the others. The hop conserves the
quark number, so the two states lie in different sectors: the crossing
is a comparison of two levels of one law, not a decay.

title: Colourless states of the empty square
label: prop:ml-square-states
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
With no matter, a colourless state of the square is a class function
of $F$, and there are as many independent ones as the group has
classes: $5$, $5$, $15$ and $17$ for the four models. Two bases are
natural. The \term{magnetic basis} is the indicator functions of the
classes, on which $B_U$ is diagonal with the values
$\beta(3-\operatorname{Re}\chi(C))$. The \term{electric basis} is the
characters $\chi_\rho(F)$, on which the electric energy is diagonal
with the values $4\kappa E(\rho)$, every link in block $\rho$. The
character table is the change of basis between them.

title: The magnetic term in the electric basis
label: thm:ml-square-matrix
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
In the electric basis the magnetic term is
\begin{align*}
B_{\rho\sigma}&=\beta\Bigl(3\delta_{\rho\sigma}-\frac{N_{\rho\sigma}+N_{\sigma\rho}}2\Bigr),\\
N_{\rho\sigma}&=\text{the multiplicity of }\rho\text{ in }\mathbf3\otimes\sigma ,
\end{align*}
and for a real triplet $N$ is symmetric and $B=\beta(3-N)$. The
columns of the character table are the eigenvectors of
$(N+N^{\mathsf T})/2$, with the class values $\operatorname{Re}\chi(C)$
as eigenvalues. For the cube group $N$ is the table of
\cref{fig:ml-square-table}, and the energy law of the empty square is
the $5\times5$ matrix $4\kappa\,\mathrm{diag}(E)+\beta(3-N)$.

title: The square to third order
label: thm:ml-square-series
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
The energy of the zero-flux state of the empty square is
\[
E_0(\beta)=3\beta-\frac{\langle(\operatorname{Re}\chi)^2\rangle}{4\kappa E_3}\,\beta^2
-\frac{\langle(\operatorname{Re}\chi)^3\rangle}{(4\kappa E_3)^2}\,\beta^3+O(\beta^4),
\]
with
\[
\langle(\operatorname{Re}\chi)^2\rangle=\frac{1+\langle\chi^2\rangle}2,\qquad
\langle(\operatorname{Re}\chi)^3\rangle=\frac{\langle\chi^3\rangle+3\langle\chi^2\bar\chi\rangle}4 .
\]
For the two real triplets both moments are $1$; for $C_3\times A_5$,
$S(1080)$ and $SU(3)$ they are $\tfrac12$ and $\tfrac14$. With
$E_3=\tfrac43$,
\begin{align*}
E_0&=3\beta-\frac{3\beta^2}{16\kappa}-\frac{9\beta^3}{256\kappa^2}+\cdots
 &&\text{for a real triplet,}\\
E_0&=3\beta-\frac{3\beta^2}{32\kappa}-\frac{9\beta^3}{1024\kappa^2}+\cdots
 &&\text{for a complex one.}
\end{align*}

title: The third-order transfer
label: thm:ml-transfer
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
On the zero-flux sector of one edge, the third-order term of the
energy law \eqref{eq:mt-energy-law} is
\[
H^{(3)}=\frac{L}{(\kappa E_3)^2},\qquad L=PV^3P,
\]
and with the cubic moment
$\langle U_{ij}U_{kl}U_{mn}\rangle=\varepsilon_{ikm}\varepsilon_{jln}/6$
of \cref{prop:mt-moments},
\[
L=\frac16\sum_{c,\,c'}\operatorname{sgn}(c)\operatorname{sgn}(c')\,
A_{c_3c'_3}A_{c_2c'_2}A_{c_1c'_1}+\text{h.c.}
\]
for a complex triplet, the sum over the six orderings $c$ of the target
colours and the six orderings $c'$ of the source colours, with
$A_{cc'}=\sum_sa^\dagger_{ycs}a_{xc's}$ as in
\cref{thm:mt-there-and-back}. For a real triplet the same weight
$\operatorname{sgn}(c)\operatorname{sgn}(c')/6$ multiplies each of the
eight words in which every factor is $A$ or $A^\dagger$.

title: What the transfer does
label: thm:ml-transfer-values
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
Let $q_x(m)$ be the four members of the quartet of
\cref{fig:mm-two-slot-invariants} at $x$, with spin
$m=\tfrac32,\tfrac12,-\tfrac12,-\tfrac32$, let $|\mathrm{full}_x\rangle$
be the full vertex, $D_x$ the pair and $H_x$ the paired holes, and
likewise at $y$; the modes are ordered $x$ before $y$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item In all five models a baryon hops as one assembly:
$L\,q_x(m)=6\,q_y(m)$ and $L\,q_y(m)=6\,q_x(m)$, the same spin and
nothing else, with amplitude $6$ for every $m$. Under the law the
transfer amplitude is $6/(\kappa E_3)^2=27/(8\kappa^2)$.
\item Let
\[
\psi_0=\tfrac12\sum_m(-1)^{3/2-m}\hat q_x(m)\hat q_y(-m)
\]
be the spin-singlet two-baryon state, with $\hat q$ the normalized
quartet members. In all five models its transfer has full-vertex
component $-12$ at each end. For a complex triplet this is the whole
image:
\[
L\psi_0=-12\bigl(|\mathrm{full}_x\rangle+|\mathrm{full}_y\rangle\bigr)
\]
\item For the real triplets two channels are added. A pair at $x$ with
a baryon at $y$ becomes a baryon at $x$ with the pair at $y$,
$L\,(D_xq_y(m))=\pm6\,q_x(m)D_y$ for every $m$, with its mirror in the
holes; and $L\psi_0$ acquires the two chain states $c_2$, $c_3$ of
\cref{fig:mm-chain} with amplitude $12$ beside the full vertices, so
that $\|L\psi_0\|=24$.
\item On the sixty-four zero-flux states of the real triplets and the
thirty-six of the complex ones, $L$ has the values of
\cref{fig:ml-transfer-spectra}, and is zero outside the sectors
listed there.
\end{enumerate}

title: A baryon on a ring and on the cube
label: prop:ml-walk
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
One baryon on a ring of four vertices has, to third order, the levels
\[
-\frac6{\kappa E_3}+\frac6{(\kappa E_3)^2}\,\{2,0,0,-2\}
=-\frac9{2\kappa}+\Bigl\{\frac{27}{4\kappa^2},\,0,\,0,\,-\frac{27}{4\kappa^2}\Bigr\},
\]
each four times over, once per spin state; on the cube of
\cref{ml:cube}, whose vertices have three neighbours,
\[
-\frac9{\kappa E_3}+\frac6{(\kappa E_3)^2}\,\{3,1,1,1,-1,-1,-1,-3\},
\]
each four times over. The braces hold the eigenvalues of the adjacency
matrix of the ring and of the cube.

title: Census of a canvas
label: thm:ml-canvas-census
chapter: A laboratory: strings, squares, and the cube
statement:
On a connected canvas with $V$ vertices, $E$ edges and $d$ slots at
every vertex, the number of colourless states with $n$ quarks is the
coefficient of $z^n$ in
\[
\sum_{C}\,|C_G(C)|^{\,E-V}\,\det(1+zg_C)^{dV},
\]
the sum over the conjugacy classes $C$ of $G$, with $g_C$ an element of
$C$ and $C_G(C)$ its centralizer. Without matter the count is
$\sum_C|C_G(C)|^{E-V}$: one state on a tree, one per class on a canvas
with a single loop, and $336\,465$ for the cube group on the cube. The
zero-flux states number the one-vertex count to the power $V$.
